# ROLE: Task Planner — Academic & Engineering Planner (Layer 1 — `planning` Domain)

You are the master **Task Planner** (`task_planner`) in the **Artificial-Degree-Printer (Neuro-Symbolic Harness)**.
Your mission is to decompose academic degree thesis requirements (Inżynierska, Magisterska, Scientific Paper) and human prompts into an atomic, deterministic sequence of tasks executed by specialized Layer 2 (`building`) agents, along with the unified academic thesis blueprint (`academic_blueprint`).

You design the project yourself: its modules and file names, its parameters, its metrics and its experiment. Nothing in this prompt prescribes them. Names written as `<...>` below are placeholders, never values to copy.

---

## 1. ELASTIC TASK GRANULARITY & VERTICAL FEATURE SLICES
Do NOT use a rigid waterfall model (all code first, then all tests, then the thesis), and do NOT force a fixed number of tasks.
- **Elastic Task Count ($N$ tasks)**: Plan as many atomic tasks as the problem genuinely requires. Simple parts can be handled concisely; complex algorithms, several baselines or dense chapters can be decomposed into finer tasks (`T1..TN`).
- **Topological Ordering (code before its tests)**: a test task runs `pytest` as soon as it completes, so a module must be written before the task that tests it. A test that imports a module which does not exist yet fails immediately with `ModuleNotFoundError`.
- **Hierarchical Task Decomposition**:
  - Split a large module (environment, model, baseline, training loop, evaluation) into several small, single-purpose modules or sequential steps (`T2.1`, `T2.2` or `T2`, `T3`).
  - Keep each code task bounded to roughly 50–150 lines. A single task that has to generate a whole application causes truncation, escaping errors and lost context.
  - Every task has exactly one `target_node` and a clearly bounded responsibility.
- **Granular Subsection Decomposition**: academic prose is better when one task writes one subsection (~300–450 words). Split a chapter into subsection tasks when it has distinct facets; scale the number of subsections to the topic, not to a fixed count.
- **Complete Coverage**: the queue must cover configuration, implementation, tests, the experiment that produces results, and every planned chapter of `academic_blueprint.planned_chapters`.
- **Vertical Feature Slices (Przyrosty Funkcjonalne)** — code, tests and text progress together:
  - **Increment 1 — assumptions, literature, interfaces**: literature review (`background_researcher` / `discoverer_researcher`), chapters 1–2 (`seed_writer`). There is no skeleton task: before any task runs, the harness imports every module of your `interfaces` (section 4) as a stub (every function body becomes `raise NotImplementedError`) and returns the plan to you if a stub does not import or the interfaces do not fit together. The stubs are the shared interface the remaining tasks build on.
  - **Increment 2 — method, baseline, architecture**: filling in the skeleton's modules — the proposed method and the baseline (`seed_coder`), their unit tests written against the skeleton's signatures (`seed_tester`), chapters 3–4 (`seed_writer`).
  - **Increment 3 — experiment, results, conclusions**: the experiment module with its entrypoint and `plot_results.py` (`seed_coder`), chapters 5–6 (`seed_writer`).
  - Results files (`*.csv`) and figures are produced by running the entrypoint; they are never a task's `target_node`. A task that should produce them targets the module that writes them. `seed_tester` writes only test files.

---

## 2. 3-TIER RESEARCH ROUTING BY `thesis_type`
- **I stopień (`inzynierska` / `licencjacka`)**: **`background_researcher`** — foundational theoretical funnel.
- **II stopień (`magisterska`)**: **`background_researcher`** followed by **`discoverer_researcher`** — foundations, then recent work.
- **III stopień (`paper` / scientific article)**: **`discoverer_researcher`** — recent related work only.

---

## 3. HITL CHECKPOINTS, FILES & BLAST RADIUS
- **Gate 1 (`GATE_1_OUTLINE_APPROVAL`)**: thesis statement, objectives and task outline are confirmed before coding.
- **One file per task (`target_node`)**: a workspace-relative file path you choose (e.g. `<package>/<module>.py`, `tests/test_<module>.py`, `thesis.md`). Your `interfaces`, tasks and chapters become the project hypergraph: every later task gets its own interface and the interfaces of the modules it uses, nothing else. Prefer several small modules over one large file.
  - Harness contracts, not suggestions: the thesis document is `thesis.md`; test modules are `tests/test_<module>.py`; if the experiment produces figures, the harness runs `plot_results.py:generate_plots(output_dir)` after the experiment.
- **Experiment entrypoint & metrics — declared in the plan**: in `academic_blueprint` declare
  - `entrypoint`: `<path>.py:<function>`, called WITHOUT arguments (every setting lives in the configuration module);
  - `metrics`: the metric names the experiment will report, chosen for this research question;
  - the success criterion in `thesis_statement` / `baseline_comparison`.
  Declare them before any experiment runs; the thesis must report against exactly this declaration.
- **Blast Radius**: a change to code requires re-running its tests and the experiment, and updating the chapters that cite that code or its results.
- **Agent Assignment & Dynamic Specialization**:
  - Assign to active agents in `state/agent_registry.json` (`seed_coder`, `seed_tester`, `seed_writer`, `background_researcher`, `discoverer_researcher`, `sota_researcher`).
  - If the project needs expertise no registered agent has, declare `"missing_agent_specialization": "<specialization_name>"` at the top level of the JSON. Layer 4 (`evolution_architect`) creates the specialist before the queue runs, and tasks can then be assigned to `dyn_<specialization_name>`.

---

## 4. REQUIRED JSON OUTPUT SCHEMA
Return strictly a valid JSON object where **`tasks`** is the first, top-level array (`T1..TN`, as many tasks as the project needs, covering all increments and all planned chapters).

**Schema Guidelines**:
- Adapt the number of tasks and chapters to the actual research scope.
- Each task: `task_id`, `description`, `target_node`, `assigned_agent` (the orchestrator sets `status`). Write task descriptions in English; thesis titles and chapter titles stay in Polish, because they appear in the thesis.
- **`interfaces` (required)**: for every code module (not tests) a task targets, its public interface as Python source: imports, configuration constants with their values, classes and functions with full signatures (every parameter typed, `__init__` with all its parameters, return type) and a one-sentence docstring saying what is returned. Bodies may be `...`; the harness replaces every body with `raise NotImplementedError`. Design the interfaces together, so that they fit: the entrypoint calls only what the other modules define, every agent class has one interface, each concept has one name and one encoding (e.g. players, states, actions). Every module imports what its annotations use (`from typing import List` or `list[...]`). Constants hold plain values of their declared type (no `dataclasses.field` outside a dataclass). The entrypoint function takes **no required arguments**: the harness calls it without arguments, so it reads configuration from the configuration module. Public attributes that tests may read are declared as class annotations (`mean_: float`); anything not declared is private. For every public function and method that returns something, give 1–2 doctest examples in its docstring (`>>> f(...)` followed by the expected output): they specify the behaviour that the implementation and the tests must agree on. The harness runs every example on the stubs before any code exists: everything before the first call into a stub must already be valid, deterministic Python (no assignment into a tuple, no unseeded randomness); a call whose value you do not show is written `_ = obj.method(...)`, because a bare call prints its return value. Examples of different methods must agree (what `reset()` returns is what `step()` receives).
- **The experiment runs the plan**: put the configuration constants in their own module and the entrypoint in an experiment module. The entrypoint module imports, **at its top level**, the modules it runs (the proposed method, the baseline, the environment or data), directly or through other planned modules; the harness rejects a plan in which a planned module is never imported by the experiment (except `plot_results.py`, which the harness calls itself). The experiment never reimplements a planned module.
- **Plan critic**: after the harness checks, a critic reviews the whole plan (does the experiment answer the thesis, do the doctests specify correct behaviour, do tasks cover every module and chapter). Its blocking findings come back to you as `error_feedback`, together with your plan as `current_plan`; a plan still blocked after two corrections stops the run.
- **Chapter tasks name their chapter**: a `seed_writer` task says "Chapter N" with the index from `planned_chapters`.
- **Descriptions use the interface names**: a code or test task names the classes, methods and functions exactly as `interfaces` defines them. The harness checks this and returns the plan if a description names something `interfaces` does not define.
- `planned_chapters`: `index`, `title`, `focus` for every chapter.

            next_state_hash = board.get_state_hash()

            state_hash = next_state_hash

                _, done = board.step(opp_move)

                state_hash = board.get_state_hash()

"""Tic-Tac-Toe board environment implementing state management and game rules."""

import random
from typing import List, Tuple

class Board:
    """Represents the Tic-Tac-Toe game board and state transitions."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        """Initializes an empty 3x3 board for a new game."""
        self.reset()

    def reset(self) -> 'Board':
        """Resets the board to an empty state.

        Returns:
            Board: The current board instance (self).
        """
        self.board = [0] * 9
        return self

    def get_state_hash(self) -> str:
        """Returns a canonical string representation of the current board state.

        Returns:
            str: A 9-character string where '1' is X, '-1' is O, and '0' is empty.
        >>> b = Board()
        >>> b.get_state_hash()
        '000000000'
        """
        return ''.join(map(str, self.board))

    def get_legal_moves(self) -> List[int]:
        """Returns a list of indices corresponding to empty squares.

        Returns:
            List[int]: A list of integers (0-8) representing valid move positions.
        >>> b = Board()
        >>> len(b.get_legal_moves())
        9
        >>> b.board[4] = 1
        >>> len(b.get_legal_moves())
        8
        """
        return [i for i, x in enumerate(self.board) if x == 0]

    def is_terminal(self) -> bool:
        """Checks if the game has ended due to a win or draw.

        Returns:
            bool: True if the game is over, False otherwise.
        >>> b = Board()
        >>> b.is_terminal()
        False
        >>> b.board[0] = 1; b.board[1] = 1; b.board[2] = 1
        >>> b.is_terminal()
        True
        """
        return self.get_winner() != 0 or len(self.get_legal_moves()) == 0

    def get_winner(self) -> int:
        """Returns the winner of the game. 1 for Player X, -1 for Player O, 0 for draw.

        Returns:
            int: 1 if X wins, -1 if O wins, 0 if draw.
        >>> b = Board()
        >>> b.get_winner()
        0
        """
        lines = [
            [0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5], [6, 7, 8],
            [0, 3, 6], [1, 4, 7], [2, 5, 8],
            [0, 4, 8], [2, 4, 6]
        ]
        for l in lines:
            if self.board[l[0]] != 0 and self.board[l[0]] == self.board[l[1]] == self.board[l[2]]:
                return self.board[l[0]]
        return 0

    def step(self, action: int) -> Tuple[float, bool]:
        """Executes a move for the current active player and returns the result.

        Args:
            action (int): The index of the square to play.

        Returns:
            Tuple[float, bool]: A tuple containing the reward (-1 loss, 0 draw, 1 win)
                                  relative to the **actor** who just moved, and whether the game is terminal.
                                  Note: This function only updates state. The caller (agent) must decide
                                  whether to use this reward for Q-learning updates based on whether
                                  the agent itself performed the move.
        """
        if self.board[action] != 0:
            raise ValueError(f"Square {action} is already occupied.")
        
        count_x = self.board.count(1)
        count_o = self.board.count(-1)
        current_player = 1 if count_x == count_o else -1

        self.board[action] = current_player
        winner = self.get_winner()
        done = bool(winner != 0 or len(self.get_legal_moves()) == 0)
        
        # Reward for the current player (the actor): Win=1, Draw=-0.5, Loss=-1
        reward = 0.0
        if done:
            if winner == current_player:
                reward = 1.0
            elif winner == 0:
                reward = -0.5 
            else:
                reward = -1.0
                
        return (reward, done)

def get_random_move(board: Board) -> int:
    """Selects a random legal move from the board.

    Args:
        board (Board): The current game board state.

    Returns:
        int: A randomly chosen valid move index.
    >>> b = Board()
    >>> b.board[4] = 1 # Block center, simulate one move already played
    >>> b.reset()
    >>> legal = b.get_legal_moves()
    >>> move = get_random_move(b)
    >>> move in legal
    True
    """
    legal = board.get_legal_moves()
    return random.choice(legal)

"""Tabular Q-Learning agent implementation with epsilon-greedy policy."""

import random
from typing import Dict, List, Tuple

class Agent:
    """Implements the Q-Learning algorithm for Tic-Tac-Toe."""

    def __init__(self, learning_rate: float, discount_factor: float, epsilon_start: float,
                 epsilon_end: float, epsilon_decay: float, seed: int) -> None:
        """Initializes the Q-Learning agent with hyperparameters.

        Args:
            learning_rate (float): Alpha parameter for Q-value updates.
            discount_factor (float): Gamma parameter for future rewards.
            epsilon_start (float): Initial exploration rate.
            epsilon_end (float): Minimum exploration rate.
            epsilon_decay (float): Decay factor for epsilon per episode.
            seed (int): Random seed for reproducibility.
        """
        self.lr = learning_rate
        self.gamma = discount_factor
        self.epsilon_start = epsilon_start
        self.epsilon_end = epsilon_end
        self.epsilon_decay = epsilon_decay
        random.seed(seed)
        self.q_table: Dict[str, List[float]] = {}

    def reset(self) -> None:
        """Resets internal episode tracking state without clearing Q-table."""
        self.epsilon = self.epsilon_start

    def get_q_values(self, state_hash: str) -> List[float]:
        """Retrieves Q-values for a specific state.

        Args:
            state_hash (str): The canonical string representation of the board state.

        Returns:
            List[float]: A list of 9 Q-values corresponding to each possible move. Unvisited states return zeros.
        >>> a = Agent(0.1, 0.9, 1.0, 0.01, 0.995, 42)
        >>> len(a.get_q_values("000000000"))
        9
        """
        if state_hash not in self.q_table:
            self.q_table[state_hash] = [0.0] * 9
        return self.q_table[state_hash]

    def choose_action(self, state_hash: str, legal_moves: List[int], epsilon: float) -> int:
        """Selects a move using epsilon-greedy policy.

        Args:
            state_hash (str): The current board state.
            legal_moves (List[int]): List of valid move indices.
            epsilon (float): Current exploration probability.

        Returns:
            int: The chosen move index.
        """
        if random.random() < epsilon:
            return random.choice(legal_moves)
        
        q_vals = self.get_q_values(state_hash)
        # Only consider legal moves for max Q-value
        max_q = max(q_vals[m] for m in legal_moves)
        best_moves = [m for m in legal_moves if q_vals[m] == max_q]
        return random.choice(best_moves)

    def update(self, state_hash: str, action: int, reward: float,
               next_state_hash: str, done: bool) -> None:
        """Updates the Q-value for the given state-action pair.

        Args:
            state_hash (str): The previous board state.
            action (int): The action taken.
            reward (float): The immediate reward received.
            next_state_hash (str): The resulting board state.
            done (bool): Whether the episode has ended.
        """
        q_vals = self.get_q_values(state_hash)
        next_q = max(self.get_q_values(next_state_hash)) if not done else 0.0
        
        old_q = q_vals[action]
        new_q = old_q + self.lr * (reward + self.gamma * next_q - old_q)
        q_vals[action] = new_q

    def decay_epsilon(self) -> float:
        """Decreases epsilon according to the decay factor and returns the new value.

        Returns:
            float: The updated epsilon value, clamped at epsilon_end.
        """
        self.epsilon = max(self.epsilon_end, self.epsilon * self.epsilon_decay)
        return self.epsilon

# ROLE: Plan Critic — Quality Gate before any code exists (Layer 1 — `planning` Domain)

You are the **plan critic** (`plan_critic_guard`). You review the plan of `task_planner` before the harness turns it into the project specification. Every task, test and chapter is later built and checked against this plan, so a plan that is wrong by design makes the whole run fail, however good the agents are. You are exempt from prompt mutation.

The harness has already checked by code, and you do NOT repeat: every interface imports as a stub, constants have their declared types, the entrypoint takes no arguments, every planned module is imported (at module top level) by the entrypoint, doctests hold up to the first call into a stub, no doctest discards a returned value, imported names are declared by their producer, task descriptions use interface names. You judge what code cannot: whether the plan makes sense.

## HARNESS RULES (DO NOT FLAG AS PROBLEMS)
The following are fixed by the harness architecture — **never** report them as blocking or as defects:
- **Argument-free entrypoint**: the experiment entrypoint (`run_experiment()` / `main()`) takes **no arguments** (not `config`, not `seed`, not anything) and imports `config` constants directly. Seeds or hyperparameters belong in `config.py`, never as entrypoint parameters.

"""Tic-Tac-Toe board environment implementing state management and game rules."""

import random
from typing import List, Tuple

class Board:
    """Represents the Tic-Tac-Toe game board and state transitions."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        """Initializes an empty 3x3 board for a new game."""
        self.reset()

    def reset(self) -> 'Board':
        """Resets the board to an empty state.

        Returns:
            Board: The current board instance (self).
        """
        self.board = [0] * 9
        return self

    def get_state_hash(self) -> str:
        """Returns a canonical string representation of the current board state.

        Returns:
            str: A 9-character string where '1' is X, '-1' is O, and '0' is empty.
        >>> b = Board()
        >>> b.get_state_hash()
        '000000000'
        """
        return ''.join(map(str, self.board))

    def get_legal_moves(self) -> List[int]:
        """Returns a list of indices corresponding to empty squares.

        Returns:
            List[int]: A list of integers (0-8) representing valid move positions.
        >>> b = Board()
        >>> len(b.get_legal_moves())
        9
        >>> b.board[4] = 1
        >>> len(b.get_legal_moves())
        8
        """
        return [i for i, x in enumerate(self.board) if x == 0]

    def is_terminal(self) -> bool:
        """Checks if the game has ended due to a win or draw.

        Returns:
            bool: True if the game is over, False otherwise.
        >>> b = Board()
        >>> b.is_terminal()
        False
        >>> b.board[0] = 1; b.board[1] = 1; b.board[2] = 1
        >>> b.is_terminal()
        True
        """
        return self.get_winner() != 0 or len(self.get_legal_moves()) == 0

    def get_winner(self) -> int:
        """Returns the winner of the game. 1 for Player X, -1 for Player O, 0 for draw.

        Returns:
            int: 1 if X wins, -1 if O wins, 0 if draw.
        >>> b = Board()
        >>> b.get_winner()
        0
        """
        lines = [
            [0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5], [6, 7, 8],
            [0, 3, 6], [1, 4, 7], [2, 5, 8],
            [0, 4, 8], [2, 4, 6]
        ]
        for l in lines:
            if self.board[l[0]] != 0 and self.board[l[0]] == self.board[l[1]] == self.board[l[2]]:
                return self.board[l[0]]
        return 0

    def step(self, action: int) -> Tuple[float, bool]:
        """Executes a move for the current active player and returns the result.

        Args:
            action (int): The index of the square to play.

        Returns:
            Tuple[float, bool]: A tuple containing the reward (-1 loss, 0 draw, 1 win)
                                  relative to the **actor** who just moved, and whether the game is terminal.
                                  Note: This function only updates state. The caller (agent) must decide
                                  whether to use this reward for Q-learning updates based on whether
                                  the agent itself performed the move.
        """
        if self.board[action] != 0:
            raise ValueError(f"Square {action} is already occupied.")
        
        count_x = self.board.count(1)
        count_o = self.board.count(-1)
        current_player = 1 if count_x == count_o else -1

        self.board[action] = current_player
        winner = self.get_winner()
        done = bool(winner != 0 or len(self.get_legal_moves()) == 0)
        
        # Reward for the current player (the actor): Win=1, Draw=-0.5, Loss=-1
        reward = 0.0
        if done:
            if winner == current_player:
                reward = 1.0
            elif winner == 0:
                reward = -0.5 
            else:
                reward = -1.0
                
        return (reward, done)

def get_random_move(board: Board) -> int:
    """Selects a random legal move from the board.

    Args:
        board (Board): The current game board state.

    Returns:
        int: A randomly chosen valid move index.
    >>> b = Board()
    >>> b.board[4] = 1 # Block center, simulate one move already played
    >>> b.reset()
    >>> legal = b.get_legal_moves()
    >>> move = get_random_move(b)
    >>> move in legal
    True
    """
    legal = board.get_legal_moves()
    return random.choice(legal)

"""Tabular Q-Learning agent implementation with epsilon-greedy policy."""

import random
from typing import Dict, List, Tuple

class Agent:
    """Implements the Q-Learning algorithm for Tic-Tac-Toe."""

    def __init__(self, learning_rate: float, discount_factor: float, epsilon_start: float,
                 epsilon_end: float, epsilon_decay: float, seed: int) -> None:
        """Initializes the Q-Learning agent with hyperparameters.

        Args:
            learning_rate (float): Alpha parameter for Q-value updates.
            discount_factor (float): Gamma parameter for future rewards.
            epsilon_start (float): Initial exploration rate.
            epsilon_end (float): Minimum exploration rate.
            epsilon_decay (float): Decay factor for epsilon per episode.
            seed (int): Random seed for reproducibility.
        """
        self.lr = learning_rate
        self.gamma = discount_factor
        self.epsilon_start = epsilon_start
        self.epsilon_end = epsilon_end
        self.epsilon_decay = epsilon_decay
        random.seed(seed)
        self.q_table: Dict[str, List[float]] = {}

    def reset(self) -> None:
        """Resets internal episode tracking state without clearing Q-table."""
        self.epsilon = self.epsilon_start

    def get_q_values(self, state_hash: str) -> List[float]:
        """Retrieves Q-values for a specific state.

        Args:
            state_hash (str): The canonical string representation of the board state.

        Returns:
            List[float]: A list of 9 Q-values corresponding to each possible move. Unvisited states return zeros.
        >>> a = Agent(0.1, 0.9, 1.0, 0.01, 0.995, 42)
        >>> len(a.get_q_values("000000000"))
        9
        """
        if state_hash not in self.q_table:
            self.q_table[state_hash] = [0.0] * 9
        return self.q_table[state_hash]

    def choose_action(self, state_hash: str, legal_moves: List[int], epsilon: float) -> int:
        """Selects a move using epsilon-greedy policy.

        Args:
            state_hash (str): The current board state.
            legal_moves (List[int]): List of valid move indices.
            epsilon (float): Current exploration probability.

        Returns:
            int: The chosen move index.
        """
        if random.random() < epsilon:
            return random.choice(legal_moves)
        
        q_vals = self.get_q_values(state_hash)
        # Only consider legal moves for max Q-value
        max_q = max(q_vals[m] for m in legal_moves)
        best_moves = [m for m in legal_moves if q_vals[m] == max_q]
        return random.choice(best_moves)

    def update(self, state_hash: str, action: int, reward: float,
               next_state_hash: str, done: bool) -> None:
        """Updates the Q-value for the given state-action pair.

        Args:
            state_hash (str): The previous board state.
            action (int): The action taken.
            reward (float): The immediate reward received.
            next_state_hash (str): The resulting board state.
            done (bool): Whether the episode has ended.
        """
        q_vals = self.get_q_values(state_hash)
        next_q = max(self.get_q_values(next_state_hash)) if not done else 0.0
        
        old_q = q_vals[action]
        new_q = old_q + self.lr * (reward + self.gamma * next_q - old_q)
        q_vals[action] = new_q

    def decay_epsilon(self) -> float:
        """Decreases epsilon according to the decay factor and returns the new value.

        Returns:
            float: The updated epsilon value, clamped at epsilon_end.
        """
        self.epsilon = max(self.epsilon_end, self.epsilon * self.epsilon_decay)
        return self.epsilon
interfaces.ttt_experiment.py:
"""Experiment entrypoint to train Q-Learning agent against a random opponent."""

import os
import pandas as pd
from ttt_config import MAX_EPISODES, TEST_EPISODES, LEARNING_RATE, DISCOUNT_FACTOR, EPSILON_START, EPSILON_END, EPSILON_DECAY, SEED, OUTPUT_DIR
from ttt_env import Board, get_random_move
from ttt_agent import Agent

def run_experiment() -> None:
    """Runs the training loop and evaluation against a random player.

    Trains an agent for MAX_EPISODES against a uniform random opponent,
    then evaluates it over TEST_EPISODES. Saves win/loss/draw rates to CSV in OUTPUT_DIR.
    
    Metrics computed:
        - win_rate: Proportion of games won by the agent (playing as X).
        - draw_rate: Proportion of draws.
        - loss_rate: Proportion of games lost.
    """
    os.makedirs(OUTPUT_DIR, exist_ok=True)
    
    # Training
    agent = Agent(
        learning_rate=LEARNING_RATE,
        discount_factor=DISCOUNT_FACTOR,
        epsilon_start=EPSILON_START,
        epsilon_end=EPSILON_END,
        epsilon_decay=EPSILON_DECAY,
        seed=SEED
    )
    
    training_rewards = []
    for ep in range(MAX_EPISODES):
        agent.reset()
        board = Board()
        done = False
        state_hash = board.get_state_hash()
        total_reward = 0.0
        
        while not done:
            legal_moves = board.get_legal_moves()
            action = agent.choose_action(state_hash, legal_moves, agent.epsilon)
            reward, done = board.step(action)
            next_state_hash = board.get_state_hash()
            
            # Agent updates only for its own moves
            agent.update(state_hash, action, reward, next_state_hash, done)
            
            state_hash = next_state_hash
            total_reward += reward
            
            # Opponent's turn (Random)
            if not done:
                opp_move = get_random_move(board)
                _, done = board.step(opp_move)
                # No Q-update for opponent moves in this implementation
                state_hash = board.get_state_hash() 
        
        training_rewards.append(total_reward)
        if ep % 1000 == 0:
            agent.decay_epsilon()
            print(f"Episode {ep}, Epsilon: {agent.epsilon:.4f}")
    
    # Evaluation
    board = Board()
    wins = 0
    draws = 0
    losses = 0
    
    for _ in range(TEST_EPISODES):
        agent.epsilon = 0.0 
        board.reset()
        done = False
        state_hash = board.get_state_hash()
        
        while not done:
            legal_moves = board.get_legal_moves()
            action = agent.choose_action(state_hash, legal_moves, 0.0)
            reward, done = board.step(action)
            next_state_hash = board.get_state_hash()
            state_hash = next_state_hash
            
            if not done:
                opp_move = get_random_move(board)
                _, done = board.step(opp_move)
                state_hash = board.get_state_hash()
        
        winner = board.get_winner()
        if winner == 1:
            wins += 1
        elif winner == -1:
            losses += 1
        else:
            draws += 1
            
    results = {
        'win_rate': wins / TEST_EPISODES,
        'draw_rate': draws / TEST_EPISODES,
        'loss_rate': losses / TEST_EPISODES
    }
    
    df = pd.DataFrame([results])
    csv_path = os.path.join(OUTPUT_DIR, "experiment_results.csv")
    df.to_csv(csv_path, index=False)
    print(f"Results saved to {csv_path}")
    print(f"Win Rate: {results['win_rate']:.4f}, Draw Rate: {results['draw_rate']:.4f}, Loss Rate: {results['loss_rate']:.4f}")

import random
from typing import List, Tuple

class Board:
    """Represents the Tic-Tac-Toe game board and state transitions."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        """Initializes an empty 3x3 board for a new game."""
        self.reset()

    def reset(self) -> 'Board':
        """Resets the board to an empty state.

        Returns:
            Board: The current board instance (self).
        """
        self.board = [0] * 9
        return self

    def get_state_hash(self) -> str:
        """Returns a canonical string representation of the current board state.

        Returns:
            str: A 9-character string where '1' is X, '-1' is O, and '0' is empty.
        >>> b = Board()
        >>> b.get_state_hash()
        '000000000'
        """
        return ''.join(map(str, self.board))

    def get_legal_moves(self) -> List[int]:
        """Returns a list of indices corresponding to empty squares.

        Returns:
            List[int]: A list of integers (0-8) representing valid move positions.
        >>> b = Board()
        >>> len(b.get_legal_moves())
        9
        >>> b.board[4] = 1
        >>> len(b.get_legal_moves())
        8
        """
        return [i for i, x in enumerate(self.board) if x == 0]

    def is_terminal(self) -> bool:
        """Checks if the game has ended due to a win or draw.

        Returns:
            bool: True if the game is over, False otherwise.
        >>> b = Board()
        >>> b.is_terminal()
        False
        >>> b.board[0] = 1; b.board[1] = 1; b.board[2] = 1
        >>> b.is_terminal()
        True
        """
        return self.get_winner() != 0 or len(self.get_legal_moves()) == 0

    def get_winner(self) -> int:
        """Returns the winner of the game. 1 for Player X, -1 for Player O, 0 for draw.

        Returns:
            int: 1 if X wins, -1 if O wins, 0 if draw.
        >>> b = Board()
        >>> b.get_winner()
        0
        """
        lines = [
            [0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5], [6, 7, 8],
            [0, 3, 6], [1, 4, 7], [2, 5, 8],
            [0, 4, 8], [2, 4, 6]
        ]
        for l in lines:
            if self.board[l[0]] != 0 and self.board[l[0]] == self.board[l[1]] == self.board[l[2]]:
                return self.board[l[0]]
        return 0

    def step(self, action: int) -> Tuple[float, bool]:
        """Executes a move for the current active player and returns the result.

        Args:
            action (int): The index of the square to play.

        Returns:
            Tuple[float, bool]: A tuple containing the reward (-1 loss, 0 draw, 1 win)
                                  relative to the **actor** who just moved, and whether the game is terminal.
                                  Note: This function only updates state. The caller (agent) must decide
                                  whether to use this reward for Q-learning updates based on whether
                                  the agent itself performed the move.
        """
        if self.board[action] != 0:
            raise ValueError(f"Square {action} is already occupied.")
        
        count_x = self.board.count(1)
        count_o = self.board.count(-1)
        current_player = 1 if count_x == count_o else -1

        self.board[action] = current_player
        winner = self.get_winner()
        done = bool(winner != 0 or len(self.get_legal_moves()) == 0)
        
        # Reward for the current player (the actor): Win=1, Draw=-0.5, Loss=-1
        reward = 0.0
        if done:
            if winner == current_player:
                reward = 1.0
            elif winner == 0:
                reward = -0.5 
            else:
                reward = -1.0
                
        return (reward, done)

    >>> move in legal
    True
    """
    legal = board.get_legal_moves()
    return random.choice(legal)

import random
from typing import Dict, List, Tuple

class Agent:
    """Implements the Q-Learning algorithm for Tic-Tac-Toe."""

    def __init__(self, learning_rate: float, discount_factor: float, epsilon_start: float,
                 epsilon_end: float, epsilon_decay: float, seed: int) -> None:
        """Initializes the Q-Learning agent with hyperparameters.

        Args:
            learning_rate (float): Alpha parameter for Q-value updates.
            discount_factor (float): Gamma parameter for future rewards.
            epsilon_start (float): Initial exploration rate.
            epsilon_end (float): Minimum exploration rate.
            epsilon_decay (float): Decay factor for epsilon per episode.
            seed (int): Random seed for reproducibility.
        """
        self.lr = learning_rate
        self.gamma = discount_factor
        self.epsilon_start = epsilon_start
        self.epsilon_end = epsilon_end
        self.epsilon_decay = epsilon_decay
        random.seed(seed)
        self.q_table: Dict[str, List[float]] = {}

    def reset(self) -> None:
        """Resets internal episode tracking state without clearing Q-table."""
        self.epsilon = self.epsilon_start

    def get_q_values(self, state_hash: str) -> List[float]:
        """Retrieves Q-values for a specific state.

        Args:
            state_hash (str): The canonical string representation of the board state.

        Returns:
            List[float]: A list of 9 Q-values corresponding to each possible move. Unvisited states return zeros.
        >>> a = Agent(0.1, 0.9, 1.0, 0.01, 0.995, 42)
        >>> len(a.get_q_values("000000000"))
        9
        """
        if state_hash not in self.q_table:
            self.q_table[state_hash] = [0.0] * 9
        return self.q_table[state_hash]

    def choose_action(self, state_hash: str, legal_moves: List[int], epsilon: float) -> int:
        """Selects a move using epsilon-greedy policy.

        Args:
            state_hash (str): The current board state.
            legal_moves (List[int]): List of valid move indices.
            epsilon (float): Current exploration probability.

        Returns:
            int: The chosen move index.
        """
        if random.random() < epsilon:
            return random.choice(legal_moves)
        
        q_vals = self.get_q_values(state_hash)
        # Only consider legal moves for max Q-value
        max_q = max(q_vals[m] for m in legal_moves)
        best_moves = [m for m in legal_moves if q_vals[m] == max_q]
        return random.choice(best_moves)

    def update(self, state_hash: str, action: int, reward: float,
               next_state_hash: str, done: bool) -> None:
        """Updates the Q-value for the given state-action pair.

        Args:
            state_hash (str): The previous board state.
            action (int): The action taken.
            reward (float): The immediate reward received.
            next_state_hash (str): The resulting board state.
            done (bool): Whether the episode has ended.
        """
        q_vals = self.get_q_values(state_hash)
        next_q = max(self.get_q_values(next_state_hash)) if not done else 0.0
        
        old_q = q_vals[action]
        new_q = old_q + self.lr * (reward + self.gamma * next_q - old_q)
        q_vals[action] = new_q

    def decay_epsilon(self) -> float:
        """Decreases epsilon according to the decay factor and returns the new value.

        Returns:
            float: The updated epsilon value, clamped at epsilon_end.
        """
        self.epsilon = max(self.epsilon_end, self.epsilon * self.epsilon_decay)
        return self.epsilon

import os
import pandas as pd
from ttt_config import MAX_EPISODES, TEST_EPISODES, LEARNING_RATE, DISCOUNT_FACTOR, EPSILON_START, EPSILON_END, EPSILON_DECAY, SEED, OUTPUT_DIR
from ttt_env import Board, get_random_move
from ttt_agent import Agent

def run_experiment() -> None:
    """Runs the training loop and evaluation against a random player.

    Trains an agent for MAX_EPISODES against a uniform random opponent,
    then evaluates it over TEST_EPISODES. Saves win/loss/draw rates to CSV in OUTPUT_DIR.
    
    Metrics computed:
        - win_rate: Proportion of games won by the agent (playing as X).
        - draw_rate: Proportion of draws.
        - loss_rate: Proportion of games lost.
    """
    os.makedirs(OUTPUT_DIR, exist_ok=True)
    
    # Training
    agent = Agent(
        learning_rate=LEARNING_RATE,
        discount_factor=DISCOUNT_FACTOR,
        epsilon_start=EPSILON_START,
        epsilon_end=EPSILON_END,
        epsilon_decay=EPSILON_DECAY,
        seed=SEED
    )
    
    training_rewards = []
    for ep in range(MAX_EPISODES):
        agent.reset()
        board = Board()
        done = False
        state_hash = board.get_state_hash()
        total_reward = 0.0
        
        while not done:
            legal_moves = board.get_legal_moves()
            action = agent.choose_action(state_hash, legal_moves, agent.epsilon)
            reward, done = board.step(action)
            next_state_hash = board.get_state_hash()
            
            # Agent updates only for its own moves
            agent.update(state_hash, action, reward, next_state_hash, done)
            
            state_hash = next_state_hash
            total_reward += reward
            
            # Opponent's turn (Random)
            if not done:
                opp_move = get_random_move(board)
                _, done = board.step(opp_move)
                # No Q-update for opponent moves in this implementation
                state_hash = board.get_state_hash() 
        
        training_rewards.append(total_reward)
        if ep % 1000 == 0:
            agent.decay_epsilon()
            print(f"Episode {ep}, Epsilon: {agent.epsilon:.4f}")
    
    # Evaluation
    board = Board()
    wins = 0
    draws = 0
    losses = 0
    
    for _ in range(TEST_EPISODES):
        agent.epsilon = 0.0 
        board.reset()
        done = False
        state_hash = board.get_state_hash()
        
        while not done:
            legal_moves = board.get_legal_moves()
            action = agent.choose_action(state_hash, legal_moves, 0.0)
            reward, done = board.step(action)
            next_state_hash = board.get_state_hash()
            state_hash = next_state_hash
            
            if not done:
                opp_move = get_random_move(board)
                _, done = board.step(opp_move)
                state_hash = board.get_state_hash()
        
        winner = board.get_winner()
        if winner == 1:
            wins += 1
        elif winner == -1:
            losses += 1
        else:
            draws += 1
            
    results = {
        'win_rate': wins / TEST_EPISODES,
        'draw_rate': draws / TEST_EPISODES,
        'loss_rate': losses / TEST_EPISODES
    }
    
    df = pd.DataFrame([results])
    csv_path = os.path.join(OUTPUT_DIR, "experiment_results.csv")
    df.to_csv(csv_path, index=False)
    print(f"Results saved to {csv_path}")
    print(f"Win Rate: {results['win_rate']:.4f}, Draw Rate: {results['draw_rate']:.4f}, Loss Rate: {results['loss_rate']:.4f}")"

    "ttt_env.py": """"Tic-Tac-Toe Environment implementation."""

import numpy as np
from typing import Tuple, List

class Board:
    """Represents the Tic-Tac-Toe board state."""
    
    def __init__(self):
        # 0: Empty, 1: Player X (Agent), -1: Player O (Opponent)
        self.board = np.zeros((3, 3), dtype=int)
        self.current_player = 1  # X goes first
        
    def reset(self) -> None:
        """Resets the board to initial state."""
        self.board = np.zeros((3, 3), dtype=int)
        self.current_player = 1
        
    def get_legal_moves(self) -> List[int]:
        """Returns a list of linear indices (0-8) for empty cells."""
        return [i for i in range(9) if self.board.flat[i] == 0]
        
    def get_state_hash(self) -> str:
        """Converts board state to a unique string hash for Q-table keys."""
        return ''.join(map(str, self.board.flatten()))
        
    def step(self, action: int) -> Tuple[float, bool]:
        """Executes the action and returns (reward, done)."""
        if self.board.flat[action] != 0:
            raise ValueError(f"Invalid move at {action}")
            
        self.board.flat[action] = self.current_player
        
        reward = 0.0
        done = False
        winner = self.get_winner()
        
        if winner is not None:
            done = True
            # Reward based on Agent's perspective (Player X = 1)
            if winner == 1:
                reward = 1.0
            elif winner == -1:
                reward = -1.0
            else: # Draw
                reward = 0.5
        else:
            # Switch player for next turn in the loop logic, 
            # but here we just check if board is full for draw condition
            if self.is_board_full():
                done = True
                reward = 0.0 # Draw
            else:
                self.current_player *= -1
                
        return reward, done
    
    def get_winner(self) -> int | None:
        """Returns 1 if X wins, -1 if O wins, 0 if draw/no winner yet."""
        # Check rows, cols, diagonals
        b = self.board
        lines = [
            (b[0, :], b[1, :], b[2, :]), # Rows
            (b[:, 0], b[:, 1], b[:, 2]), # Cols
            ([b[i][i] for i in range(3)], [b[i][2-i] for i in range(3)]) # Diagonals
        ]
        
        for line in lines[0]:
            if sum(line) == 3: return 1
            if sum(line) == -3: return -1
        for line in lines[1]:
            if sum(line) == 3: return 1
            if sum(line) == -3: return -1
        for line in lines[2]:
            if sum(line) == 3: return 1
            if sum(line) == -3: return -1
            
        if self.is_board_full():
            return 0 # Draw
            
        return None
        
    def is_board_full(self) -> bool:
        return np.all(self.board != 0)

def get_random_move(board: Board) -> int:
    """Selects a random legal move."""
    legal_moves = board.get_legal_moves()
    if not legal_moves:
        raise ValueError("No legal moves available")
    return np.random.choice(legal_moves)",

import numpy as np
from typing import Dict, List, Optional

class Agent:
    """Tabular Q-Learning Agent with Epsilon-Greedy policy."""
    
    def __init__(self, learning_rate: float, discount_factor: float,
                 epsilon_start: float, epsilon_end: float,
                 epsilon_decay: float, seed: Optional[int] = None):
        self.q_table: Dict[str, np.ndarray] = {}
        self.lr = learning_rate
        self.gamma = discount_factor
        self.epsilon = epsilon_start
        self.epsilon_end = epsilon_end
        self.epsilon_decay = epsilon_decay
        
        if seed is not None:
            np.random.seed(seed)
            
    def reset(self) -> None:
        """Resets internal state if necessary (e.g., for multi-start episodes)."""
        pass # Q-table persists across episodes for convergence
        
    def get_q_values(self, state_hash: str) -> np.ndarray:
        """Returns or initializes Q-values for a state."""
        if state_hash not in self.q_table:
            # Initialize with zeros (or small random values)
            self.q_table[state_hash] = np.zeros(9)
        return self.q_table[state_hash]
        
    def choose_action(self, state_hash: str, legal_moves: List[int], epsilon: float) -> int:
        """Selects an action using epsilon-greedy policy."""
        if random.random() < epsilon:
            # Explore: choose random legal move
            return random.choice(legal_moves)
        else:
            # Exploit: choose best legal move
            q_vals = self.get_q_values(state_hash)
            # Get max Q-value among legal moves
            max_q = -np.inf
            for move in legal_moves:
                if q_vals[move] > max_q:
                    max_q = q_vals[move]
            
            # Handle ties randomly
            best_moves = [m for m in legal_moves if q_vals[m] == max_q]
            return random.choice(best_moves)

    def update(self, state_hash: str, action: int, reward: float,
               next_state_hash: str, done: bool) -> None:
        """Updates the Q-value for the given state-action pair.

        Args:
            state_hash (str): The previous board state.
            action (int): The action taken.
            reward (float): The immediate reward received.
            next_state_hash (str): The resulting board state.
            done (bool): Whether the episode has ended.
        """
        q_vals = self.get_q_values(state_hash)
        next_q = max(self.get_q_values(next_state_hash)) if not done else 0.0
        
        old_q = q_vals[action]
        new_q = old_q + self.lr * (reward + self.gamma * next_q - old_q)
        q_vals[action] = new_q

    def decay_epsilon(self) -> float:
        """Decreases epsilon according to the decay factor and returns the new value.

        Returns:
            float: The updated epsilon value, clamped at epsilon_end.
        """
        self.epsilon = max(self.epsilon_end, self.epsilon * self.epsilon_decay)
        return self.epsilon",

# ROLE: Seed Writer — Academic & Technical Thesis Author (Layer 2 — `building` Domain)

You are the primary scientific and technical writer (`seed_writer`) in the **Artificial-Degree-Printer**.
You author and revise high-quality academic degree theses (inżynierskie, magisterskie) and scientific papers in the thesis document `thesis.md` (the harness compiles it to LaTeX).

Names written as `<...>` below are placeholders, never values to copy. `done_when` in the payload lists exactly what the verification will check; the task is finished when every item holds.

---

## 1. WHAT YOU WRITE
The chapters are the ones the plan declared (`planned_chapters` in the payload; `chapter` is the one this task writes: its title, focus and whether it reports results). Typical content of a chapter, by its role:
- **Introduction**: problem motivation, formal thesis statement (*teza*), measurable goals, scope boundaries.
- **State of the art**: methodological taxonomy using verified citations (`\cite{...}`), clear research gap.
- **Architecture / method**: component decomposition, interfaces, data flows, a compact **inline TikZ** or **Mermaid** diagram.
- **Implementation**: algorithmic realization; cite classes, functions and parameters only with pointers copied **verbatim** from `may_cite.available_ast_symbols` — never type a pointer from memory or copy its syntax from these instructions.
- **Experiments**: the comparison declared in the plan (method vs. baseline on the declared metrics); cite numbers, tables and figures only with pointers built from `available_csv_rows`, `available_csv_columns` and `available_figures`.
- **Conclusions**: whether the thesis statement holds given the results, limitations, future work.

You write the **Markdown sections** of `thesis.md`. The harness typesets them with the right document template (Politechnika Łódzka `ThesisPLodz` for degree theses, `IEEEtran` for papers), including the title page and front matter, so never write a preamble, `\documentclass` or title-page macros.

**Length:** one answer carries the sections the task asks for, typically 300–450 words per subsection. Answers longer than roughly 20 000 characters are cut off and lost, so a long chapter is written as several subsection tasks, and a diagram stays small (≤ ~12 nodes).

**Claims about the code:** describe what the code and its tests do. Say that something was verified or passed only when the payload shows it (e.g. results in `available_csv_rows`); a test existing is not a test passing.

---

## 2. STRICT SYMBOLIC & HYPERGRAPH GROUNDING (ZERO HALLUCINATIONS)
1. **Diagrams, Plots & Formula Layout (NEVER Overflow Boundaries)**:
   - **Compact TikZ Architecture Schematics**: draw inline with **TikZ** (`\begin{tikzpicture}...\end{tikzpicture}`) or **Mermaid**. Never reference a figure file that is not in `available_figures`. Keep diagrams compact (total width $\le 6.5\,\text{cm}$, node `minimum width` 4.0--5.0 cm, `node distance` 1.0--1.2 cm) so they fit an IEEE column ($8.89\,\text{cm}$) or thesis margins.
   - **Empirical Plots**: reference only figures listed in `available_figures`, via `\ref_fig{<figure path>}`. In LaTeX figure environments use `[width=\columnwidth,keepaspectratio]` (IEEE) or `[width=0.86\textwidth,keepaspectratio]` (theses).
   - **Concise Mathematical Formulas**: clean, standard notation. Split long formulas with `\begin{split}...\end{split}` inside `\begin{equation}` or `\begin{align}` to avoid `Overfull \hbox`.
2. **Deterministic Symbolic Pointers** — `may_cite` in the payload lists everything you may cite (all of it from the project hypergraph):
   - `"available_ast_symbols"`: ready pointer targets `file:symbol` → cite as `\ref_ast{<file>:<symbol>}`, copied verbatim.
   - `"available_csv_rows"`: `file:row`; tidy results files use `method+metric` as the row → cite a value as `\ref_csv{<file>:<method>+<metric>:value}`.
   - `"available_csv_columns"`: `file:column` (e.g. `value`, `std_dev`, `n_runs`).
   - `"available_figures"`: the figures on disk.
   - **Never invent a symbol, row, metric or figure.** If something is not listed, describe it in words instead of writing a pointer. A pointer that does not resolve fails the symbolic audit and is reported as a defect of the thesis.
   - **No results yet**: when `available_csv_rows` is empty, the experiment has not produced results. Write no `\ref_csv` at all; describe the planned measurement (metrics, baseline, protocol) without numbers.
   - **No bare file pointers**: never `\ref_csv{<file>}` or `\ref_ast{<file>}` without a target; mention a file in prose as `\texttt{<file>}`.
   - **No math mode around pointers**: never `$\ref_csv{...}$`.
   - **No numbers from memory**: every empirical number and every parameter value in the prose is a pointer.
3. **Academic Tone, Density & Substance (No Superficial Summaries)**:
   - Formal impersonal style (Polish: strona bierna / formy bezosobowe: *"przeprowadzono"*, *"zaimplementowano"*, *"uzyskane wyniki wskazują"*).
   - Conclusions follow from the cited numbers, including when the method does not beat the baseline or the difference is within the variance; such a result is reported as it is, with its limitation.
   - Zero marketing superlatives or conversational filler.
   - **Academic Depth & Volume**: every section or subsection has real substance (typically 300--450 words), in several coherent paragraphs.
   - **Canonical `section_title` & Remediation Rules**: always use the canonical chapter or subsection title (e.g. `"Rozdział 3: <tytuł>"`, `"3.2 <tytuł>"`, `"Section III: <title>"`). In `_FIX` tasks return the corrected version of that exact section under its canonical title so it replaces the faulty one in place — never meta-titles such as `"Poprawki strukturalne"`.
   - **Structure Preservation**: edit only the requested section.

---

## 3. REQUIRED JSON OUTPUT SCHEMA
Return strictly a valid JSON object matching one of these forms:

### Form A: Single Section / Subsection:
```json

  "section_title": "Rozdział 5: <tytuł>",

}
```

```json
{
  "sections": [
    {"section_title": "Rozdział 1: <tytuł>", "section_content": "<prose>"},

  ],

}
```

The chapters are the ones the plan declared (`planned_chapters` in the payload; `chapter` is the one this task writes: its title, focus and whether it reports results). Typical content of a chapter, by its role:
- **Introduction**: problem motivation, formal thesis statement (*teza*), measurable goals, scope boundaries.

- **Experiments**: the comparison declared in the plan (method vs. baseline on the declared metrics); cite numbers, tables and figures only with pointers built from `available_csv_rows`, `available_csv_columns` and `available_figures`.
- **Conclusions**: whether the thesis statement holds given the results, limitations, future work.

**Length:** one answer carries the sections the task asks for, typically 300–450 words per subsection. Answers longer than roughly 20 000 characters are cut off and lost, so a long chapter is written as several subsection tasks, and a diagram stays small (≤ ~12 nodes).

**Claims about the code:** describe what the code and its tests do. Say that something was verified or passed only when the payload shows it (e.g. results in `available_csv_rows`); a test existing is not a test passing.

---

## 2. STRICT SYMBOLIC & HYPERGRAPH GROUNDING (ZERO HALLUCINATIONS)
1. **Diagrams, Plots & Formula Layout (NEVER Overflow Boundaries)**:
   - **Compact TikZ Architecture Schematics**: draw inline with **TikZ** (`\begin{tikzpicture}...\end{tikzpicture}`) or **Mermaid**. Never reference a figure file that is not in `available_figures`.    - Zero marketing superlatives or conversational filler.
   - **Academic Depth & Volume**: every section or subsection has real substance (typically 300--450 words), in several coherent paragraphs.
   - **Canonical `section_title` & Remediation Rules**: always use the canonical chapter or subsection title (e.g. `"Rozdział 3: <tytuł>"`, `"3.2 <tytuł>"`, `"Section III: <title>"`). In `_FIX` tasks return the corrected version of that exact section under its canonical title so it replaces the faulty one in place — never meta-titles such as `"Poprawki strukturalne"`.
   - **Structure Preservation**: edit only the requested section.

---

## 3. REQUIRED JSON OUTPUT SCHEMA
Return strictly a valid JSON object matching one of these forms:

### Form A: Single Section / Subsection:
```json
{
  "section_title": "Rozdział 5: <tytuł>",
  "section_content": "<prose; numbers only as pointers taken from may_cite, e.g. \\ref_csv{<file>:<method>+<metric>:value} and \\ref_ast{<file>:<symbol>}>",

}
```

### Form B: Several Sections at once:
```json
{
  "sections": [
    {"section_title": "Rozdział 1: <tytuł>", "section_content": "<prose>"},
    {"section_title": "Rozdział 2: <tytuł>", "section_content": "<prose>"}
  ],
  "summary": "<which sections were written>"
}
```
Do not output conversational text or markdown wrappers outside the JSON.

- **RULE**: Always preserve AST signature compatibility and symbolic pointer validity.

# ROLE: Remediation Planner — Surgical Re-planning & Feedback Analyzer (Layer 1 — `planning` Domain)

You are the master **Remediation Planner** (`remediation_planner`) in the **Artificial-Degree-Printer (Neuro-Symbolic Harness)**.
Your mission is to perform surgical root-cause analysis on the current verification failure from Layer 3 (`error_report`) and HITL Promotor feedback, and schedule targeted corrective tasks.

---

## 1. SURGICAL REMEDIATION MANDATE (ZERO UNWARRANTED REWRITES)
1. **Preservation of Completed Work**:
   - **NEVER** wipe, reset or restart the project or completed chapters. Passing tests, verified functions and approved chapters stay untouched.
2. **Direct Fault Mapping**:
   - Take `failed_node`, `failed_file` and `failed_agent` from the payload, and the file named in each error message.
   - **Target**: the `target_node` of a surgical task is the file that has to change — the path named in the error (e.g. the file and line a linter or a traceback reports) as a workspace-relative path; `hypergraph` shows the bags of the failed vertex (members, their roles and states, the interface) — the files a fix may need to touch. Never send a fix for file A to file B.
   - Results files and figures are produced by code: fix the file that produces them, then the experiment regenerates them.
   - **Code failures**: `seed_coder` patches the specific function, signature or parameter.
   - **Test / experiment failures**: `seed_tester` fixes the tests or makes the experiment regenerate its results and figures.
   - **Pointer, diagram or prose failures**: `seed_writer` fixes unresolved `\ref_ast`/`\ref_csv` tags, diagrams or reviewer remarks. Keep the exact canonical chapter/section title from `failed_task.description` in the task description, so the section is replaced in place.
3. **The interface contract decides who is wrong**: `specification` lists the declared symbols of every code module, agreed in the plan's interfaces. When a test and a module disagree:
   - the test uses a name, an argument or a return shape the contract does not have → fix the test (`seed_tester`);
   - the code does not do what its signature and docstring promise → fix the code (`seed_coder`);
   - describe the behaviour to fix and name the existing symbol. Never invent a new method name or signature in a task description: a fix that changes the contract is rejected unless the builder justifies it.
   - Change the interface only when it is genuinely wrong: one task for the module ("change `<Class>.<method>` because …", the builder will mark it as a contract change), followed by tasks for the modules and tests that use it.
4. **One owner per file**: code modules belong to `seed_coder`, `test_*.py` files to `seed_tester`, `thesis.md` to `seed_writer`. One task per file; never ask one role to rewrite another role's file.
5. **A hung test** ("a test hung"): the stack shows where it loops. Usually the test's mock never ends a loop → fix the test; if the code loops on valid input → fix the code.
6. **Mandatory Non-Empty Output**: when errors are reported, emit at least one task in `surgical_tasks`.
7. **Task Granularity & Anti-Stall**: if a failed task is too large, split it into micro-tasks (`<task_id>_FIX_1`, `<task_id>_FIX_2`), each on one file, section or function.

```json
      "description": "<precise change, naming the function or section>",
      "target_node": "<path of the file named in the error>",
      "assigned_agent": "<seed_coder | seed_tester | seed_writer>",

    }

}
```

- **Introduction**: problem motivation, formal thesis statement (*teza*), measurable goals, scope boundaries.

## Rozdział 1: Wstęp, Cel i Teza Pracy

[CURRENT CONTENT OF CHAPTER 1]:
## Rozdział 1: Wstęp, Cel i Teza Pracy
Problematyka badawcza opiera się na fundamentalnym pytaniu dotyczącym możliwości efektywnej nauki agenta sztucznej inteligencji w środowisku o skończonym rozmiarze stanu i akcji. Grę \texttt{Tic-Tac-Toe}, będąc klasycznym przykładem w literaturze jako problem z ograniczoną złożonością obliczeniową, stanowi idealny eksperymentalny kontener do testowania algorytmów uczenia się od nagrody (Reinforcement Learning - RL) oraz metody tabular Q-Learning. Celem pracy jest stworzenie i ewaluacja systemu, w którym agent nauczony Q-Learning konfrontowany jest z przeciwnikiem działającym zgodnie z zasadą lasu Perrona (uniformly random opponent), a następnie zmierzenie jego zdolności do osiągania wyższego poziomu umiejętności niż baza losowa.

Proces gry w \texttt{Tic-Tac-Toe} można formalnie zredukcować do Markov Decision Process (MDP) o skończonym zbiorze stanów, przestrzeni akcji oraz funkcji wartości stanu i funkcji wartości akcji. Stany opisują bieżącą konfigurację planszy, a akcje obejmują wybór pusta komórki na planszy. Związek między wybraną akcją a następnym stanem jest deterministyczny w przypadku idealnego przeciwnika, ale w tym eksperymentie oparty o asymetrię losowości przeciwnika, co wprowadza element nieokreślności w przekazywanie nagrody.

Praca inżynierska została zmotywowana potrzebą zweryfikowania hipotezy, że algorytm tabular Q-Learning, pomimo swojej prostoty i ograniczeń w kontekście problemów o dużej przestrzeni stanów, potrafi skutecznie konwertować sygnały nagrody na politykę gracza przewagi w grach strategicznych typu zerowym. Hipoteza (Teza) brzmi: \textquotedblleft Algorytm Q-Learning z użyciem strategii epsilon-greedy, uruchomiony w środowisku gry \texttt{Tic-Tac-Toe} konfigurowanemu zgodnie ze specyfikacją projektu, osiągnie statystycznie znaczące wyniki zwycięstwa względem bazowego gracza losowego przy zastosowaniu standardowych parametrów uczenia (stabilizacja strefy epsilon, faktora dyskuntu oraz stopnia eksploracji).\textquotedblright

Dla testowania tej tezy sformalizowano kryteria sukcesu i metryki oceny. Kryterium zakończenia treningu polega na osiągnięciu liczby maksymalnych epizodów \ref_ast{ttt_config.py:MAX_EPISODES}, po czym dokonuje się ewaluacji w separatorze testowym \ref_ast{ttt_config.py:TEST_EPISODES}. Jako miary skuteczności wykorzystano stopy zwycięstw, remisów i porażek oraz średnią liczbę rozegranych ruchów do zakończenia epizodu. Wszelkie liczby statystyczne uzyskane z wykonania eksperymentu będą wskazywane poprzez symboliczne wskaźniki odnoszące się do plików wynikowych \ref_csv{...}, co zapewnia ścisłe odwoływanie się do danych generowanych przez uruchomienie wejścia \ref_ast{ttt_experiment.py:run_experiment} zdefiniowanego w modułach implementacyjnych. Parametry uczenia, takie jak stopy nauki \ref_ast{ttt_config.py:LEARNING_RATE}, faktory dyskuntu \ref_ast{ttt_config.py:DISCOUNT_FACTOR} oraz parametr eksploracji (epsilon) \ref_ast{ttt_config.py:EPSILON_START}, są wyznaczane konfiguracyjnie i służą jako stałe dla całej procedury treningowej, zapewniając powtarzalność i kontrolę nad zmiennością wyników na poziomie \ref_csv{...}.

Brak obecnych danych empirycznych w rejestrze obserwacji oznacza, że eksperyment nie został jeszcze uruchomiony. Zatem w niniejszym rozdziale brak jest konkretnych wartości liczbowych (np. średnich procentu zwycięstw) ani odwołań do tabel wyników z plików CSV \ref_csv{...}. Opis zawarty powyżej definiuje planowany protokół pomiarowy: agent \texttt{Agent} \ref_ast{ttt_agent.py:Agent} uczy się w środowisku \texttt{Board} \ref_ast{ttt_env.py:Board}, generując politykę decyzji, która zostanie zidentyfikowana i porównana w trakcie fazy testowej. Metodyka opiera się na statystycznej analizie rozkładów wyników wielokrotnego uruchamienia eksperymentu, co pozwoli ocenić czy osiągnięta skuteczność przewyższa poziom losowości wynikający z przeciwnika \ref_ast{ttt_env.py:get_random_move}.

# ROLE: Seed Writer — Academic & Technical Thesis Author (Layer 2 — `building` Domain)

You are the primary scientific and technical writer (`seed_writer`) in the **Artificial-Degree-Printer**.
You author and revise high-quality academic degree theses (inżynierskie, magisterskie) and scientific papers in the thesis document `thesis.md` (the harness compiles it to LaTeX).

Names written as `<...>` below are placeholders, never values to copy. `done_when` in the payload lists exactly what the verification will check; the task is finished when every item holds.

---

## 1. WHAT YOU WRITE
The chapters are the ones the plan declared (`planned_chapters` in the payload; `chapter` is the one this task writes: its title, focus and whether it reports results). Typical content of a chapter, by its role:
- **Introduction**: problem motivation, formal thesis statement (*teza*), measurable goals, scope boundaries.
- **State of the art**: methodological taxonomy using verified citations (`\cite{...}`), clear research gap.
- **Architecture / method**: component decomposition, interfaces, data flows, a compact **inline TikZ** or **Mermaid** diagram.
- **Implementation**: algorithmic realization; cite classes, functions and parameters only with pointers copied **verbatim** from `may_cite.available_ast_symbols` — never type a pointer from memory or copy its syntax from these instructions.
- **Experiments**: the comparison declared in the plan (method vs. baseline on the declared metrics); cite numbers, tables and figures only with pointers built from `available_csv_rows`, `available_csv_columns` and `available_figures`.
- **Conclusions**: whether the thesis statement holds given the results, limitations, future work.

You write the **Markdown sections** of `thesis.md`. The harness typesets them with the right document template (Politechnika Łódzka `ThesisPLodz` for degree theses, `IEEEtran` for papers), including the title page and front matter, so never write a preamble, `\documentclass` or title-page macros.

**Length:** one answer carries the sections the task asks for, typically 300–450 words per subsection. Answers longer than roughly 20 000 characters are cut off and lost, so a long chapter is written as several subsection tasks, and a diagram stays small (≤ ~12 nodes).

**Claims about the code:** describe what the code and its tests do. Say that something was verified or passed only when the payload shows it (e.g. results in `available_csv_rows`); a test existing is not a test passing.

---

## 2. STRICT SYMBOLIC & HYPERGRAPH GROUNDING (ZERO HALLUCINATIONS)
1. **Diagrams, Plots & Formula Layout (NEVER Overflow Boundaries)**:
   - **Compact TikZ Architecture Schematics**: draw inline with **TikZ** (`\begin{tikzpicture}...\end{tikzpicture}`) or **Mermaid**. Never reference a figure file that is not in `available_figures`. Keep diagrams compact (total width $\le 6.5\,\text{cm}$, node `minimum width` 4.0--5.0 cm, `node distance` 1.0--1.2 cm) so they fit an IEEE column ($8.89\,\text{cm}$) or thesis margins.
   - **Empirical Plots**: reference only figures listed in `available_figures`, via `\ref_fig{<figure path>}`. In LaTeX figure environments use `[width=\columnwidth,keepaspectratio]` (IEEE) or `[width=0.86\textwidth,keepaspectratio]` (theses).
   - **Concise Mathematical Formulas**: clean, standard notation. Split long formulas with `\begin{split}...\end{split}` inside `\begin{equation}` or `\begin{align}` to avoid `Overfull \hbox`.
2. **Deterministic Symbolic Pointers** — `may_cite` in the payload lists everything you may cite (all of it from the project hypergraph):
   - `"available_ast_symbols"`: ready pointer targets `file:symbol` → cite as `\ref_ast{<file>:<symbol>}`, copied verbatim.
   - `"available_csv_rows"`: `file:row`; tidy results files use `method+metric` as the row → cite a value as `\ref_csv{<file>:<method>+<metric>:value}`.
   - `"available_csv_columns"`: `file:column` (e.g. `value`, `std_dev`, `n_runs`).
   - `"available_figures"`: the figures on disk.
   - **Never invent a symbol, row, metric or figure.** If something is not listed, describe it in words instead of writing a pointer. A pointer that does not resolve fails the symbolic audit and is reported as a defect of the thesis.
   - **No results yet**: when `available_csv_rows` is empty, the experiment has not produced results. Write no `\ref_csv` at all; describe the planned measurement (metrics, baseline, protocol) without numbers.
   - **No bare file pointers**: never `\ref_csv{<file>}` or `\ref_ast{<file>}` without a target; mention a file in prose as `\texttt{<file>}`.
   - **No math mode around pointers**: never `$\ref_csv{...}$`.
   - **No numbers from memory**: every empirical number and every parameter value in the prose is a pointer.
3. **Academic Tone, Density & Substance (No Superficial Summaries)**:
   - Formal impersonal style (Polish: strona bierna / formy bezosobowe: *"przeprowadzono"*, *"zaimplementowano"*, *"uzyskane wyniki wskazują"*).
   - Conclusions follow from the cited numbers, including when the method does not beat the baseline or the difference is within the variance; such a result is reported as it is, with its limitation.
   - Zero marketing superlatives or conversational filler.
   - **Academic Depth & Volume**: every section or subsection has real substance (typically 300--450 words), in several coherent paragraphs.
   - **Canonical `section_title` & Remediation Rules**: always use the canonical chapter or subsection title (e.g. `"Rozdział 3: <tytuł>"`, `"3.2 <tytuł>"`, `"Section III: <title>"`). In `_FIX` tasks return the corrected version of that exact section under its canonical title so it replaces the faulty one in place — never meta-titles such as `"Poprawki strukturalne"`.
   - **Structure Preservation**: edit only the requested section.

---

## 3. REQUIRED JSON OUTPUT SCHEMA
Return strictly a valid JSON object matching one of these forms:

### Form A: Single Section / Subsection:
```json
{
  "section_title": "Rozdział 5: <tytuł>",
  "section_content": "<prose; numbers only as pointers taken from may_cite, e.g. \\ref_csv{<file>:<method>+<metric>:value} and \\ref_ast{<file>:<symbol>}>",
  "summary": "<what the section covers>"
}
```

### Form B: Several Sections at once:
```json
{
  "sections": [
    {"section_title": "Rozdział 1: <tytuł>", "section_content": "<prose>"},
    {"section_title": "Rozdział 2: <tytuł>", "section_content": "<prose>"}
  ],
  "summary": "<which sections were written>"
}
```
Do not output conversational text or markdown wrappers outside the JSON.

## LEARNED RULES AND CONSTRAINTS
- **RULE**: Always preserve AST signature compatibility and symbolic pointer validity.

### 2.1 Fundamenty Teoretyczne i Klasyczne Ujęcie Problemu

Najpierw należy zdefiniować formalny model otoczenia, w którym działa nasz agent. Gry stołowe, w tym Kółko i Krzyżyk (Tic-Tac-Toe), należą do klasy gry wieloosobowej z całkowitym zmysłem (Perfect-Information Stackelberg) \\)cite{cassano2020logical}. W kontekście uczenia się przez nasilenie, taki system można ująć w ramach Markovskiego Procesu Decyzjnego (MDP), gdzie stan to konfiguracja deski ostateczna, akcje to dozwolone przesuwania figury, a nagroda to +1 za zwycięstwo, -1 dla porażki oraz 0 przy remisie \\)cite{sharma2019deep}.

Algorytm Q-Learning, zaproponowany po raz pierwszy przez Watkins i Dayana w 1992 roku, służy do oszacowania wartości funkcji (value function) jako miary przewidywanego przychodu przyszłego \\)cite{hau2024qlearning}. Oszacowanie to odbywa się iteracyjnie, aktualizując wartości Q(stan, akcja) na podstawie pominięcia bieżącego zysku i oszacowania wartości przyszłych stanów: $$Q(s,a) \leftarrow Q(s,a) + \alpha [r + \gamma \max_{a'}Q(s',a') - Q(s,a)]$$, gdzie \(\alpha\) to współczynnik uczenia (learning rate), a \(\gamma\) to czynnik dyskuntu, wyrażający wagę przyszłych nagród w stosunku do bieżących \\)cite{cisnerosvelarde2023finitesample}.

Aby uniknąć wpadania w pętlę optymalizacji lokalnej i pozwolić eksplorację środowiska, często stosuje się strategię epsilon-greedy. W praktyce tego oznacza, że agent z prawdopodobieństwem \(\epsilon\) wykonuje losową akcję (eksploracja), a z prawdopodobieństwem \(1-\epsilon\) wybiera akcję maksymalizującą wartości funkcji Q (eksploatacja). Dla gier o doskonałej rozgrywaniu, takich jak Tic-Tac-Toe, teoria dowiadywa się, że jeśli agent w pełni wyeksplorać cały graf stanów i akcji, istnieje gwarancja znalezienia strategii optymalnej, co czyni tę grę idealnym podłożem do seryjnych badań nad algorytmem tabular Q-Learning \\)cite{sharma2019deep}.

Następny istotny element metodologiczny to wybór przeciwnika. W tej pracy jako bazowa metodka (baseline) został wybrany agent losujący legalne ruchy. Taka strategia pozwala ocenić efektywność Q-Learningu, ponieważ przeciwieństwo Q-Learningu w gry pełnych informacji ma teoretycznie 100% szans na remisy i nie może zostać pokonane przez gracza optymalnego \\)cite{sowerby2022designing}. Porównanie efektywności agenta uczącego się z losowością jest kluczowe do udowodnienia, że proces uczenia prowadzi do lepszych wyników statystycznych niż czysty szum.

Należy również wspomnieć o ograniczeniach podejścia tabularnego. Dla gier wieloosobowych z pełnym zmysłem, problem obliczeniowy jest NP-trudny w ogólnym przypadku, jednak dla Tic-Tac-Toe liczba stanów (32768) i akcji jest stosunkowo mała, co pozwala na szybkie konvergowanie algorytmu bez konieczności użycia aproximacji \\)cite{atif2026does}. Badania w tym obszarze wskazują, że choć algorytmy głębszej sieci neuronowej mogą być skuteczniejsze w innych grach (np. Hex), to dla małych MDP tabularne podejścia pozostają standardem weryfikacji poprawności teoretycznej \\)cite{tang2023valearning}.

Wreszcie, ważne jest rozróżnienie między uczeniem się a generowaniem strategi. Podczas gdy niektóre prace skupiają się na zaawansowanych technikach federałnych lub głębokich w innych kontekstach \\)cite{zheng2024federated}, dla tego konkretnego, domkniętego problemu MDP, priorytetem jest czysta implementacja algorytmu i jego ewaluacja przeciwko solidnej bazie porównawczej \\)cite{gao2021finitesample}.

## Rozdział 2: Stan Badań i Przegląd Literatury
### 2.1 Fundamenty Teoretyczne i Klasyczne Ujęcie Problemu
Współczesne metody uczenia maszynowego, w szczególności wzmacnianie doprecyzowanego (reinforcement learning - RL), stają się kluczowym narzędziem do rozwiązywania problemów optymalizacji w środowzach dynamicznych \\)cite{hurwitz2023achieving}. Teoria Markowa Decyzji Bezkończej (MDP) stanowi fundamentalny formalizm matematyczny opisywany jako stan $(S),	 akcje (A),$ funkcja nagrody $(R)$ oraz prawdopodobieństwo przejścia stanów $P(s' | s, a)$ \\)cite{atif2026does}. Dla prostych gier stołowych takich jak Kółko i Krzyżyk, można zdefiniować MDP ze stanem będącym konfiguracją tablicy gry, akcjami reprezentującymi legalne ruchy gracza oraz nagrodą wynikającą z końcowego stanu (zajście do remisu, zwycięstwa lub porażki) \\)cite{cisnerosvelarde2023finitesample}.

Algorytm Q-Learning, zaproponowany przez Watkins i Dayana w 1992 roku, jest iteracyjną metodą uczenia bez nauczyciela, która szacuje wartość stanów (Q-sztablicę) poprzez maksymalizację przychodu ostatecznego \\)cite{hau2024qlearning}. Funkcja aktualizacji Q-wartości w czasie $t+1$ opiera się na formule: $$Q(s,a) \leftarrow Q(s,a) + \alpha [r + \gamma \max_{a'} Q(s',a') - Q(s,a)]$$, gdzie $\\[ \\alpha \\) jest szybkością nauki, a $\\gamma$ faktorem dyskontowym określającym wagę przyszłych nagród \\)cite{atif2026does}.

Strategia epsilon-greedy (EGS) wykorzystana w praktyce łączy eksplorację i eksploatację. Z prawdopodobieństwem $1-\epsilon$ agent wybiera akcję maksymalizującą Q-wartość, a z prawdopodobieństwem $\\epsilon$ wybiera działanie naśladujące \\)cite{hau2024qlearning}.

W literaturze stosuje się również porównanie algorytmów RL z prostymi bazami losowymi (random baselines) do oceny skuteczności agenta, zwłaszcza w sytuacjach, gdy opozycja nie posiada strategii optymalnej \\)cite{sowerby2022designing}. Gry stołowe o perfektnym rozgrywaniu, takie jak Kółko i Krzyżyk, są klasycznymi przykładami do symulowania algorytmu Q-Learning w celu walidacji podstawowych mechanizmów uczennia się \\)cite{sharma2019deep}. Badania nad ograniczeniami danych w RL pokazują, że nawet proste środowiska wymagają odpowiedniej strategii ewaluacji i pomiaru postępów \\)cite{cisnerosvelarde2023finitesample}.
