  "section_content": "Współczesne metody uczenia maszynowego, w szczególności wzmacnianie doprecyzowane (reinforcement learning - RL), stają się kluczowym narzędziem do rozwiązywania problemów optymalizacji w środowzach dynamicznych \cite{hurwitz2023achieving}. Teoria Markowa Decyzji Bezkończej (MDP) stanowi fundamentalny formalizm matematyczny opisujący systemy jako stan $(S), akcje (A)$, funkcję nagrody $(R)$ oraz prawdopodobieństwo przejścia stanów $P(s' | s, a)$ \cite{atif2026does}. Dla prostych gier stołowych takich jak Kółko i Krzyżyk, można zdefiniować MDP ze stanem będącym konfiguracją tablicy gry, akcjami reprezentującymi legalne ruchy gracza oraz nagrodą wynikającą z końcowego stanu (zajście do remisu, zwycięstwa lub porażki) \cite{cisnerosvelarde2023finitesample}.

Algorytm Q-Learning, zaproponowany przez Watkins i Dayana w 1992 roku, jest iteracyjną metodą uczenia bez nauczyciela, która szacuje wartość stanów (Q-sztablicę) poprzez maksymalizację przychodu ostatecznego \cite{hau2024qlearning}. Funkcja aktualizacji Q-wartości w czasie $t+1$ opiera się na formule: $$Q(s,a) \leftarrow Q(s,a) + \alpha [r + \gamma \max_{a'} Q(s',a') - Q(s,a)]$$, gdzie $\\[ \\alpha \\) jest szybkością nauki, a $\\gamma$ faktorem dyskontowym określającym wagę przyszłych nagród \cite{atif2026does}.

Strategia epsilon-greedy (EGS) wykorzystana w praktyce łączy eksplorację i eksploatację. Z prawdopodobieństwem $1-\epsilon$ agent wybiera akcję maksymalizującą Q-wartość, a z prawdopodobieństwem $\\epsilon$ wybiera działanie naśladujące \cite{hau2024qlearning}.

W literaturze stosuje się również porównanie algorytmów RL z prostymi bazami losowymi (random baselines) do oceny skuteczności agenta, zwłaszcza w sytuacjach, gdy opozycja nie posiada strategii optymalnej \cite{sowerby2022designing}. Gry stołowe o perfektnym rozgrywaniu, takie jak Kółko i Krzyżyk, są klasycznymi przykładami do symulowania algorytmu Q-Learning w celu walidacji podstawowych mechanizmów uczennia się \cite{sharma2019deep}. Badania nad ograniczeniami danych w RL pokazują, że nawet proste środowiska wymagają odpowiedniej strategii ewaluacji i pomiaru postępów \cite{cisnerosvelarde2023finitesample}.

W ramach niniejszej pracy, teoria Q-Learning zostanie zastosowana do środowiska gry typu MDP, gdzie agent dokłada decyzję na podstawie tablicy Q. Proces uczenia się będzie realizowany poprzez iteracje z wykorzystaniem parametrów określonych w konfiguracji eksperymentu, takich jak \texttt{ttt_config.py:LEARNING_RATE}, \texttt{ttt_config.py:DISCOUNT_FACTOR} oraz \texttt{ttt_config.py:EPSILON_START}. Wartości Q będą estymowane na podstawie doświadczeń zgromadzonych w trakcie interakcji z otoczeniem, a końcowy model agenta będzie oparta na strukturze reprezentowanej przez klasę \texttt{ttt_agent.py:Agent}, która implementuje logikę aktualizacji i selekcji akcji. Badania nad ograniczeniami danych w RL wskazują konieczność przeprowadzenia serii wielokrotnych symulacji, przy czym liczba rozgrywek testowych zostanie określona jako \texttt{ttt_config.py:TEST_EPISODES}, co pozwoli na uzyskanie statystycznie niezmiennego wyniku końcowego.

Aby zweryfikować efektywność uczonego modelu, agent zostanie porównany z bazą losową \cite{sowerby2022designing}. Baseline ten będzie symulował opozycję, która w każdym kroku wybiera legalne ruchy zgodnie z rozkładem jednostajnym. W kontekście tej pracy, agent Q-Learning zostanie porównany z bazowym strukturalnym (basem losowym) \cite{sowerby2022designing}. Wyniki porównania, w tym statystyki zwycięstw, remisów i strat, zostaną przedstawione w tablicy wynikowej przygotowanej przez modul wywołujący \texttt{ttt_experiment.py:run_experiment}, który koordynuje cykl treningowy oraz symulacje testowe oparte na środowisku \texttt{ttt_env.py:get_random_move}. Obecnie nie są dostępne dane eksperymentalne, dlatego poniższa sekcja zawiera wyłącznie opis teoretyczny planowanych procedur i architektury badawczej."
  }

## Rozdział 1: Wstęp, Cel i Teza Pracy
## Rozdział 2: Stan Badań i Przegląd Literatury

[CURRENT CONTENT OF CHAPTER 2]:
## Rozdział 2: Stan Badań i Przegląd Literatury
Współczesne metody uczenia maszynowego, w szczególności wzmacnianie doprecyzowane (reinforcement learning - RL), stają się kluczowym narzędziem do rozwiązywania problemów optymalizacji w środowzach dynamicznych \cite{hurwitz2023achieving}. Teoria Markowa Decyzji Bezkończej (MDP) stanowi fundamentalny formalizm matematyczny opisujący systemy jako stan $(S), akcje (A)$, funkcję nagrody $(R)$ oraz prawdopodobieństwo przejścia stanów $P(s' | s, a)$ \cite{atif2026does}. Dla prostych gier stołowych takich jak Kółko i Krzyżyk, można zdefiniować MDP ze stanem będącym konfiguracją tablicy gry, akcjami reprezentującymi legalne ruchy gracza oraz nagrodą wynikającą z końcowego stanu (zajście do remisu, zwycięstwa lub porażki) \cite{cisnerosvelarde2023finitesample}.

Algorytm Q-Learning, zaproponowany przez Watkins i Dayana w 1992 roku, jest iteracyjną metodą uczenia bez nauczyciela, która szacuje wartość stanów (Q-sztablicę) poprzez maksymalizację przychodu ostatecznego \cite{hau2024qlearning}. Funkcja aktualizacji Q-wartości w czasie $t+1$ opiera się na formule: $$Q(s,a) \leftarrow Q(s,a) + \alpha [r + \gamma \max_{a'} Q(s',a') - Q(s,a)]$$, gdzie $\\[ \\alpha \\) jest szybkością nauki, a $\\gamma$ faktorem dyskontowym określającym wagę przyszłych nagród \cite{atif2026does}.

Strategia epsilon-greedy (EGS) wykorzystana w praktyce łączy eksplorację i eksploatację. Z prawdopodobieństwem $1-\epsilon$ agent wybiera akcję maksymalizującą Q-wartość, a z prawdopodobieństwem $\\epsilon$ wybiera działanie naśladujące \cite{hau2024qlearning}.

W literaturze stosuje się również porównanie algorytmów RL z prostymi bazami losowymi (random baselines) do oceny skuteczności agenta, zwłaszcza w sytuacjach, gdy opozycja nie posiada strategii optymalnej \cite{sowerby2022designing}. Gry stołowe o perfektnym rozgrywaniu, takie jak Kółko i Krzyżyk, są klasycznymi przykładami do symulowania algorytmu Q-Learning w celu walidacji podstawowych mechanizmów uczennia się \cite{sharma2019deep}. Badania nad ograniczeniami danych w RL pokazują, że nawet proste środowiska wymagają odpowiedniej strategii ewaluacji i pomiaru postępów \cite{cisnerosvelarde2023finitesample}.

W ramach niniejszej pracy, teoria Q-Learning zostanie zastosowana do środowiska gry typu MDP, gdzie agent dokłada decyzję na podstawie tablicy Q. Proces uczenia się będzie realizowany poprzez iteracje z wykorzystaniem parametrów określonych w konfiguracji eksperymentu, takich jak \texttt{ttt_config.py:LEARNING_RATE}, \texttt{ttt_config.py:DISCOUNT_FACTOR} oraz \texttt{ttt_config.py:EPSILON_START}. Wartości Q będą estymowane na podstawie doświadczeń zgromadzonych w trakcie interakcji z otoczeniem, a końcowy model agenta będzie oparta na strukturze reprezentowanej przez klasę \texttt{ttt_agent.py:Agent}, która implementuje logikę aktualizacji i selekcji akcji. Badania nad ograniczeniami danych w RL wskazują konieczność przeprowadzenia serii wielokrotnych symulacji, przy czym liczba rozgrywek testowych zostanie określona jako \texttt{ttt_config.py:TEST_EPISODES}, co pozwoli na uzyskanie statystycznie niezmiennego wyniku końcowego.

Aby zweryfikować efektywność uczonego modelu, agent zostanie porównany z bazą losową \cite{sowerby2022designing}. Baseline ten będzie symulował opozycję, która w każdym kroku wybiera legalne ruchy zgodnie z rozkładem jednostajnym. W kontekście tej pracy, agent Q-Learning zostanie porównany z bazowym strukturalnym (basem losowym) \cite{sowerby2022designing}. Wyniki porównania, w tym statystyki zwycięstw, remisów i strat, zostaną przedstawione w tablicy wynikowej przygotowanej przez modul wywołujący \texttt{ttt_experiment.py:run_experiment}, który koordynuje cykl treningowy oraz symulacje testowe oparte na środowisku \texttt{ttt_env.py:get_random_move}. Obecnie nie są dostępne dane eksperymentalne, dlatego poniższa sekcja zawiera wyłącznie opis teoretyczny planowanych procedur i architektury badawczej.

"""Tic-Tac-Toe board environment implementing state management and game rules."""
import random
from typing import List, Tuple

class Board:
    """Represents the Tic-Tac-Toe game board and state transitions."""
    board: 'object'

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        """Initializes an empty 3x3 board for a new game."""
        raise NotImplementedError

    def reset(self) -> 'Board':
        """Resets the board to an empty state.

        Returns:
            Board: The current board instance (self).
        """
        raise NotImplementedError

    def get_state_hash(self) -> str:
        """Returns a canonical string representation of the current board state.

        Returns:
            str: A 9-character string where '1' is X, '-1' is O, and '0' is empty.
        >>> b = Board()
        >>> b.get_state_hash()
        '000000000'
        """
        raise NotImplementedError

    def get_legal_moves(self) -> List[int]:
        """Returns a list of indices corresponding to empty squares.

        Returns:
            List[int]: A list of integers (0-8) representing valid move positions.
        >>> b = Board()
        >>> len(b.get_legal_moves())
        9
        >>> b.board[4] = 1
        >>> len(b.get_legal_moves())
        8
        """
        raise NotImplementedError

    def is_terminal(self) -> bool:
        """Checks if the game has ended due to a win or draw.

        Returns:
            bool: True if the game is over, False otherwise.
        >>> b = Board()
        >>> b.is_terminal()
        False
        >>> b.board[0] = 1; b.board[1] = 1; b.board[2] = 1
        >>> b.is_terminal()
        True
        """
        raise NotImplementedError

    def get_winner(self) -> int:
        """Returns the winner of the game. 1 for Player X, -1 for Player O, 0 for draw.

        Returns:
            int: 1 if X wins, -1 if O wins, 0 if draw.
        >>> b = Board()
        >>> b.get_winner()
        0
        """
        raise NotImplementedError

    def step(self, action: int) -> Tuple[float, bool]:
        """Executes a move for the current active player and returns the result.

        Args:
            action (int): The index of the square to play.

        Returns:
            Tuple[float, bool]: A tuple containing the reward (-1 loss, 0 draw, 1 win)
                                  relative to the **actor** who just moved, and whether the game is terminal.
                                  Note: This function only updates state. The caller (agent) must decide
                                  whether to use this reward for Q-learning updates based on whether
                                  the agent itself performed the move.
        """
        raise NotImplementedError

def get_random_move(board: Board) -> int:
    """Selects a random legal move from the board.

    Args:
        board (Board): The current game board state.

    Returns:
        int: A randomly chosen valid move index.
    >>> b = Board()
    >>> b.board[4] = 1 # Block center, simulate one move already played
    >>> b.reset()
    >>> legal = b.get_legal_moves()
    >>> move = get_random_move(b)
    >>> move in legal
    True
    """
    raise NotImplementedError

    """Initializes an empty 3x3 board for a new game.

    Sets up the internal representation of the board as a list of length 9.

    Attributes:
        board: A list of integers representing the 3x3 board.
    """
    self.board = [0] * 9

def reset(self) -> 'Board':
    """Resets the board to an empty state.

    Replaces the current board configuration with a fresh empty one and returns self.

    Returns:
        Board: The current board instance (self).
    """
    self.board = [0] * 9
    return self

def get_state_hash(self) -> str:
    """Returns a canonical string representation of the current board state.

    Converts the internal list into a 9-character string where '1' is X, '-1' is O, and '0' is empty.

    Returns:
        str: A 9-character string representing the board state.
    """
    return ''.join(str(x) for x in self.board)

def get_legal_moves(self) -> List[int]:
    """Returns a list of indices corresponding to empty squares.

    Identifies all positions on the board that do not yet have a value.

    Returns:
        List[int]: A list of integers (0-8) representing valid move positions.
    """
    return [i for i, val in enumerate(self.board) if val == 0]

def is_terminal(self) -> bool:
    """Checks if the game has ended due to a win or draw.

    Evaluates all possible lines on the board for completed sequences.

    Returns:
        bool: True if the game is over (win or draw), False otherwise.
    """
    # Check for full rows, columns, and diagonals
    lines = [
        [0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5], [6, 7, 8],
        [0, 3, 6], [1, 4, 7], [2, 5, 8],
        [0, 4, 8], [2, 4, 6]
    ]
    
    for line in lines:
        if self.board[line[0]] == self.board[line[1]] == self.board[line[2]]:
            return True
    
    # Check for draw (no empty squares)
    if not any(val == 0 for val in self.board):
        return True
    
    return False

def get_winner(self) -> int:
    """Returns the winner of the game. 1 for Player X, -1 for Player O, 0 for draw.

    Determines the outcome based on the current board configuration.

    Returns:
        int: 1 if X wins, -1 if O wins, 0 if draw.
    """
    if self.is_terminal():
        # Check for winner by comparing all lines
        lines = [
            [0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5], [6, 7, 8],
            [0, 3, 6], [1, 4, 7], [2, 5, 8],
            [0, 4, 8], [2, 4, 6]
        ]
        
        first_val = self.board[lines[0][0]]
        if first_val != 0:
            for line in lines:
                if self.board[line[0]] == first_val and self.board[line[1]] == first_val and self.board[line[2]] == first_val:
                    return first_val
        
        # If we reach here, it must be a draw (since is_terminal was True)
        return 0
    
    return 0

def step(self, action: int) -> Tuple[float, bool]:
    """Executes a move for the current active player and returns the result.

    Updates the board state based on the given action index. The caller must track
    whose turn it is to determine if they are the actor or opponent for reward calculation.

    Args:
        action (int): The index of the square to play (0-8).

    Returns:
        Tuple[float, bool]: A tuple containing the reward (-1 loss, 0 draw, 1 win)
                            relative to the **actor** who just moved, and whether the game is terminal.
                            Note: This function only updates state. The caller (agent) must decide
                            whether to use this reward for Q-learning updates based on whether
                            the agent itself performed the move.
    """
    if action not in self.get_legal_moves():
        raise ValueError(f"Invalid action {action}. Legal moves: {self.get_legal_moves()}")
    
    # Update board state: We assume X (1) is always Player 1 and O (-1) is Player 2
    # The actor parameter is external to this class, so we just update the board.
    self.board[action] = 1
    
    reward = -1 if self.get_winner() == -1 else (0 if self.get_winner() == 0 else 1)
    terminal = self.is_terminal()
    
    return float(reward), terminal

def get_random_move(board: Board) -> int:
    """Selects a random legal move from the board.

    Picks a random index from the list of available moves provided by the board.

    Args:
        board (Board): The current game board state.

    Returns:
        int: A randomly chosen valid move index.
    """
    legal_moves = board.get_legal_moves()
    if not legal_moves:
        raise ValueError("No legal moves available. Game is full.")
    
    return random.choice(legal_moves)

"""Tic-Tac-Toe board environment implementing state management and game rules."""
import random
from typing import List, Tuple

class Board:
    """Represents the Tic-Tac-Toe game board and state transitions."""
    board: 'object'

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        """Initializes an empty 3x3 board for a new game.

    Sets up the internal representation of the board as a list of length 9.

    Attributes:
        board: A list of integers representing the 3x3 board.
    """
        self.board = [0] * 9

    def reset(self) -> 'Board':
        """Resets the board to an empty state.

    Replaces the current board configuration with a fresh empty one and returns self.

    Returns:
        Board: The current board instance (self).
    """
        self.board = [0] * 9
        return self

    def get_state_hash(self) -> str:
        """Returns a canonical string representation of the current board state.

    Converts the internal list into a 9-character string where '1' is X, '-1' is O, and '0' is empty.

    Returns:
        str: A 9-character string representing the board state.
    """
        return ''.join((str(x) for x in self.board))

    def get_legal_moves(self) -> List[int]:
        """Returns a list of indices corresponding to empty squares.

    Identifies all positions on the board that do not yet have a value.

    Returns:
        List[int]: A list of integers (0-8) representing valid move positions.
    """
        return [i for i, val in enumerate(self.board) if val == 0]

    def is_terminal(self) -> bool:
        """Checks if the game has ended due to a win or draw.

    Evaluates all possible lines on the board for completed sequences.

    Returns:
        bool: True if the game is over (win or draw), False otherwise.
    """
        lines = [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5], [6, 7, 8], [0, 3, 6], [1, 4, 7], [2, 5, 8], [0, 4, 8], [2, 4, 6]]
        for line in lines:
            if self.board[line[0]] == self.board[line[1]] == self.board[line[2]]:
                return True
        if not any((val == 0 for val in self.board)):
            return True
        return False

    def get_winner(self) -> int:
        """Returns the winner of the game. 1 for Player X, -1 for Player O, 0 for draw.

    Determines the outcome based on the current board configuration.

    Returns:
        int: 1 if X wins, -1 if O wins, 0 if draw.
    """
        if self.is_terminal():
            lines = [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5], [6, 7, 8], [0, 3, 6], [1, 4, 7], [2, 5, 8], [0, 4, 8], [2, 4, 6]]
            first_val = self.board[lines[0][0]]
            if first_val != 0:
                for line in lines:
                    if self.board[line[0]] == first_val and self.board[line[1]] == first_val and (self.board[line[2]] == first_val):
                        return first_val
            return 0
        return 0

    def step(self, action: int) -> Tuple[float, bool]:
        """Executes a move for the current active player and returns the result.

    Updates the board state based on the given action index. The caller must track
    whose turn it is to determine if they are the actor or opponent for reward calculation.

    Args:
        action (int): The index of the square to play (0-8).

    Returns:
        Tuple[float, bool]: A tuple containing the reward (-1 loss, 0 draw, 1 win)
                            relative to the **actor** who just moved, and whether the game is terminal.
                            Note: This function only updates state. The caller (agent) must decide
                            whether to use this reward for Q-learning updates based on whether
                            the agent itself performed the move.
    """
        if action not in self.get_legal_moves():
            raise ValueError(f'Invalid action {action}. Legal moves: {self.get_legal_moves()}')
        self.board[action] = 1
        reward = -1 if self.get_winner() == -1 else 0 if self.get_winner() == 0 else 1
        terminal = self.is_terminal()
        return (float(reward), terminal)

def get_random_move(board: Board) -> int:
    """Selects a random legal move from the board.

    Picks a random index from the list of available moves provided by the board.

    Args:
        board (Board): The current game board state.

    Returns:
        int: A randomly chosen valid move index.
    """
    legal_moves = board.get_legal_moves()
    if not legal_moves:
        raise ValueError('No legal moves available. Game is full.')
    return random.choice(legal_moves)

        """Initializes an empty 3x3 board for a new game."""
        self.reset()

    def reset(self) -> 'Board':
        """Resets the board to an empty state.

        Returns:
            Board: The current board instance (self).
        """
        self.board = [0] * 9
        return self

    def get_state_hash(self) -> str:
        """Returns a canonical string representation of the current board state.

        Returns:
            str: A 9-character string where '1' is X, '-1' is O, and '0' is empty.
        >>> b = Board()
        >>> b.get_state_hash()
        '000000000'
        """
        return ''.join(map(str, self.board))

    def get_legal_moves(self) -> List[int]:
        """Returns a list of indices corresponding to empty squares.

        Returns:
            List[int]: A list of integers (0-8) representing valid move positions.
        >>> b = Board()
        >>> len(b.get_legal_moves())
        9
        >>> b.board[4] = 1
        >>> len(b.get_legal_moves())
        8
        """
        return [i for i, x in enumerate(self.board) if x == 0]

    def is_terminal(self) -> bool:
        """Checks if the game has ended due to a win or draw.

        Returns:
            bool: True if the game is over, False otherwise.
        >>> b = Board()
        >>> b.is_terminal()
        False
        >>> b.board[0] = 1; b.board[1] = 1; b.board[2] = 1
        >>> b.is_terminal()
        True
        """
        return self.get_winner() != 0 or len(self.get_legal_moves()) == 0

    def get_winner(self) -> int:
        """Returns the winner of the game. 1 for Player X, -1 for Player O, 0 for draw.

        Returns:
            int: 1 if X wins, -1 if O wins, 0 if draw.
        >>> b = Board()
        >>> b.get_winner()
        0
        """
        lines = [
            [0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5], [6, 7, 8],
            [0, 3, 6], [1, 4, 7], [2, 5, 8],
            [0, 4, 8], [2, 4, 6]
        ]
        for l in lines:
            if self.board[l[0]] != 0 and self.board[l[0]] == self.board[l[1]] == self.board[l[2]]:
                return self.board[l[0]]
        return 0

    def step(self, action: int) -> Tuple[float, bool]:
        """Executes a move for the current active player and returns the result.

        Args:
            action (int): The index of the square to play.

        Returns:
            Tuple[float, bool]: A tuple containing the reward (-1 loss, 0 draw, 1 win)
                                  relative to the **actor** who just moved, and whether the game is terminal.
                                  Note: This function only updates state. The caller (agent) must decide
                                  whether to use this reward for Q-learning updates based on whether
                                  the agent itself performed the move.
        """
        if self.board[action] != 0:
            raise ValueError(f"Square {action} is already occupied.")
        
        count_x = self.board.count(1)
        count_o = self.board.count(-1)
        current_player = 1 if count_x == count_o else -1

        self.board[action] = current_player
        winner = self.get_winner()
        done = bool(winner != 0 or len(self.get_legal_moves()) == 0)
        
        # Reward for the current player (the actor): Win=1, Draw=-0.5, Loss=-1
        reward = 0.0
        if done:
            if winner == current_player:
                reward = 1.0
            elif winner == 0:
                reward = -0.5 
            else:
                reward = -1.0
                
        return (reward, done)

def get_random_move(board: Board) -> int:
    """Selects a random legal move from the board.

    Args:
        board (Board): The current game board state.

    Returns:
        int: A randomly chosen valid move index.

    >>> b.reset()
    >>> legal = b.get_legal_moves()
    >>> move = get_random_move(b)
    >>> move in legal
    True
    """
    legal = board.get_legal_moves()
    return random.choice(legal)

"""Tic-Tac-Toe board environment implementing state management and game rules."""
import random
from typing import List, Tuple

class Board:
    """Represents the Tic-Tac-Toe game board and state transitions."""
    board: 'object'

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        """Initializes an empty 3x3 board for a new game.

    Sets up the internal representation of the board as a list of length 9.

    Attributes:
        board: A list of integers representing the 3x3 board.
    """
        self.board = [0] * 9

    def reset(self) -> 'Board':
        """Resets the board to an empty state.

Replaces the current board configuration with a fresh empty one and returns self.

Returns:
    Board: The current board instance (self).
"""
        self.board = [0] * 9
        return self

    def get_state_hash(self) -> str:
        """Returns a canonical string representation of the current board state.

    Converts the internal list into a 9-character string where '1' is X, '-1' is O, and '0' is empty.

    Returns:
        str: A 9-character string representing the board state.
    """
        return ''.join((str(x) for x in self.board))

    def get_legal_moves(self) -> List[int]:
        """Returns a list of indices corresponding to empty squares.

    Identifies all positions on the board that do not yet have a value.

    Returns:
        List[int]: A list of integers (0-8) representing valid move positions.
    """
        return [i for i, val in enumerate(self.board) if val == 0]

    def is_terminal(self) -> bool:
        """Checks if the game has ended due to a win or draw.

Evaluates all possible lines on the board for completed sequences.

Returns:
    bool: True if the game is over (win or draw), False otherwise.
"""
        lines = [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5], [6, 7, 8], [0, 3, 6], [1, 4, 7], [2, 5, 8], [0, 4, 8], [2, 4, 6]]
        for line in lines:
            if self.board[line[0]] == self.board[line[1]] == self.board[line[2]] != 0:
                return True
        if not any((val == 0 for val in self.board)):
            return True
        return False

    def get_winner(self) -> int:
        """Returns the winner of the game. 1 for Player X, -1 for Player O, 0 for draw.

    Determines the outcome based on the current board configuration.

    Returns:
        int: 1 if X wins, -1 if O wins, 0 if draw.
    """
        if self.is_terminal():
            lines = [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5], [6, 7, 8], [0, 3, 6], [1, 4, 7], [2, 5, 8], [0, 4, 8], [2, 4, 6]]
            first_val = self.board[lines[0][0]]
            if first_val != 0:
                for line in lines:
                    if self.board[line[0]] == first_val and self.board[line[1]] == first_val and (self.board[line[2]] == first_val):
                        return first_val
            return 0
        return 0

    def step(self, action: int) -> Tuple[float, bool]:
        """Executes a move for the current active player and returns the result.

    Updates the board state based on the given action index. The caller must track
    whose turn it is to determine if they are the actor or opponent for reward calculation.

    Args:
        action (int): The index of the square to play (0-8).

    Returns:
        Tuple[float, bool]: A tuple containing the reward (-1 loss, 0 draw, 1 win)
                            relative to the **actor** who just moved, and whether the game is terminal.
                            Note: This function only updates state. The caller (agent) must decide
                            whether to use this reward for Q-learning updates based on whether
                            the agent itself performed the move.
    """
        if action not in self.get_legal_moves():
            raise ValueError(f'Invalid action {action}. Legal moves: {self.get_legal_moves()}')
        self.board[action] = 1
        reward = -1 if self.get_winner() == -1 else 0 if self.get_winner() == 0 else 1
        terminal = self.is_terminal()
        return (float(reward), terminal)

def get_random_move(board: Board) -> int:
    """Selects a random legal move from the board.

    Picks a random index from the list of available moves provided by the board.

    Args:
        board (Board): The current game board state.

    Returns:
        int: A randomly chosen valid move index.
    """
    legal_moves = board.get_legal_moves()
    if not legal_moves:
        raise ValueError('No legal moves available. Game is full.')
    return random.choice(legal_moves)

"""Tabular Q-Learning agent implementation with epsilon-greedy policy."""
import random
from typing import Dict, List, Tuple

class Agent:
    """Implements the Q-Learning algorithm for Tic-Tac-Toe."""
    lr: 'object'
    gamma: 'object'
    epsilon_start: 'object'
    epsilon_end: 'object'
    epsilon_decay: 'object'
    q_table: 'Dict[str, List[float]]'
    epsilon: 'object'

    def __init__(self, learning_rate: float, discount_factor: float, epsilon_start: float, epsilon_end: float, epsilon_decay: float, seed: int) -> None:
        """Initializes the Q-Learning agent with hyperparameters.

        Args:
            learning_rate (float): Alpha parameter for Q-value updates.
            discount_factor (float): Gamma parameter for future rewards.
            epsilon_start (float): Initial exploration rate.
            epsilon_end (float): Minimum exploration rate.
            epsilon_decay (float): Decay factor for epsilon per episode.
            seed (int): Random seed for reproducibility.
        """
        raise NotImplementedError

    def reset(self) -> None:
        """Resets internal episode tracking state without clearing Q-table."""
        raise NotImplementedError

    def get_q_values(self, state_hash: str) -> List[float]:
        """Retrieves Q-values for a specific state.

        Args:
            state_hash (str): The canonical string representation of the board state.

        Returns:
            List[float]: A list of 9 Q-values corresponding to each possible move. Unvisited states return zeros.
        >>> a = Agent(0.1, 0.9, 1.0, 0.01, 0.995, 42)
        >>> len(a.get_q_values("000000000"))
        9
        """
        raise NotImplementedError

    def choose_action(self, state_hash: str, legal_moves: List[int], epsilon: float) -> int:
        """Selects a move using epsilon-greedy policy.

        Args:
            state_hash (str): The current board state.
            legal_moves (List[int]): List of valid move indices.
            epsilon (float): Current exploration probability.

        Returns:
            int: The chosen move index.
        """
        raise NotImplementedError

    def update(self, state_hash: str, action: int, reward: float, next_state_hash: str, done: bool) -> None:
        """Updates the Q-value for the given state-action pair.

        Args:
            state_hash (str): The previous board state.
            action (int): The action taken.
            reward (float): The immediate reward received.
            next_state_hash (str): The resulting board state.
            done (bool): Whether the episode has ended.
        """
        raise NotImplementedError

    def decay_epsilon(self) -> float:
        """Decreases epsilon according to the decay factor and returns the new value.

        Returns:
            float: The updated epsilon value, clamped at epsilon_end.
        """
        raise NotImplementedError

    Args:
        learning_rate (float): Alpha parameter for Q-value updates.
        discount_factor (float): Gamma parameter for future rewards.
        epsilon_start (float): Initial exploration rate.
        epsilon_end (float): Minimum exploration rate.
        epsilon_decay (float): Decay factor for epsilon per episode.
        seed (int): Random seed for reproducibility.
    """
        self.lr: float = learning_rate
        self.gamma: float = discount_factor
        self.epsilon_start: float = epsilon_start
        self.epsilon_end: float = epsilon_end
        self.epsilon_decay: float = epsilon_decay
        self.seed: int = seed
        self.q_table: Dict[str, List[float]] = {}
        self.epsilon: float = epsilon_start
        random.seed(seed)

def reset(self) -> None:
    """Resets internal episode tracking state without clearing Q-table.

    Note: The Q-table persists across episodes to utilize experience, which is standard for Tabular Q-Learning.
    """
        self.epsilon = self.epsilon_start

def get_q_values(self, state_hash: str) -> List[float]:
    """Retrieves Q-values for a specific state.

    Args:
        state_hash (str): The canonical string representation of the board state.

    Returns:
        List[float]: A list of 9 Q-values corresponding to each possible move. Unvisited states return zeros.
    
    >>> a = Agent(0.1, 0.9, 1.0, 0.01, 0.995, 42)
    >>> len(a.get_q_values("000000000"))

            self.q_table[state_hash] = [0.0 for _ in range(9)]
        return self.q_table[state_hash]

    """Updates the Q-value for the given state-action pair.

    Args:
        state_hash (str): The previous board state.
        action (int): The action taken.
        reward (float): The immediate reward received.
        next_state_hash (str): The resulting board state.
        done (bool): Whether the episode has ended.
    """
        q_current = self.get_q_values(state_hash)[action]
        next_q_values = self.get_q_values(next_state_hash)
        max_next_q = max(next_q_values) if next_q_values else 0.0
        self.q_table[state_hash][action] = q_current + self.lr * (reward + self.gamma * max_next_q - q_current)

        discount_factor (float): Gamma parameter for future rewards.
        epsilon_start (float): Initial exploration rate.
        epsilon_end (float): Minimum exploration rate.
        epsilon_decay (float): Decay factor for epsilon per episode.
        seed (int): Random seed for reproducibility.
    """

        self.gamma: float = discount_factor
        self.epsilon_start: float = epsilon_start
        self.epsilon_end: float = epsilon_end
        self.epsilon_decay: float = epsilon_decay
        self.seed: int = seed
        self.q_table: Dict[str, List[float]] = {}
        self.epsilon: float = epsilon_start
        random.seed(seed)

    def reset(self) -> None:
        """Resets internal episode tracking state without clearing Q-table.

"""Tabular Q-Learning agent implementation with epsilon-greedy policy."""
import random
from typing import Dict, List, Tuple

class Agent:
    """Implements the Q-Learning algorithm for Tic-Tac-Toe."""
    lr: 'object'
    gamma: 'object'
    epsilon_start: 'object'
    epsilon_end: 'object'
    epsilon_decay: 'object'
    q_table: 'Dict[str, List[float]]'
    epsilon: 'object'

    def __init__(self, learning_rate: float=0.1, discount_factor: float=0.9, epsilon_start: float=1.0, epsilon_end: float=0.01, epsilon_decay: float=0.995, seed: int=42) -> None:
        """Initializes the Q-Learning agent with hyperparameters.

    Args:
        learning_rate (float): Alpha parameter for Q-value updates.
        discount_factor (float): Gamma parameter for future rewards.
        epsilon_start (float): Initial exploration rate.
        epsilon_end (float): Minimum exploration rate.
        epsilon_decay (float): Decay factor for epsilon per episode.
        seed (int): Random seed for reproducibility.
    """
        self.lr: float = learning_rate
        self.gamma: float = discount_factor
        self.epsilon_start: float = epsilon_start
        self.epsilon_end: float = epsilon_end
        self.epsilon_decay: float = epsilon_decay
        self.seed: int = seed
        self.q_table: Dict[str, List[float]] = {}
        self.epsilon: float = epsilon_start
        random.seed(seed)

    def reset(self) -> None:
        """Resets internal episode tracking state without clearing Q-table.

    Note: The Q-table persists across episodes to utilize experience, which is standard for Tabular Q-Learning.
    """
        self.epsilon = self.epsilon_start

    def get_q_values(self, state_hash: str) -> List[float]:
        """Retrieves Q-values for a specific state.

    Args:
        state_hash (str): The canonical string representation of the board state.

    Returns:
        List[float]: A list of 9 Q-values corresponding to each possible move. Unvisited states return zeros.

    >>> a = Agent(0.1, 0.9, 1.0, 0.01, 0.995, 42)
    >>> len(a.get_q_values("000000000"))
    9
    """
        if state_hash not in self.q_table:
            self.q_table[state_hash] = [0.0 for _ in range(9)]
        return self.q_table[state_hash]

    def choose_action(self, state_hash: str, legal_moves: List[int], epsilon: float) -> int:
        """Selects a move using epsilon-greedy policy.

    Args:
        state_hash (str): The current board state.
        legal_moves (List[int]): List of valid move indices.
        epsilon (float): Current exploration probability.

    Returns:
        int: The chosen move index.
    """
        if random.random() < epsilon:
            return random.choice(legal_moves)
        else:
            q_values = self.get_q_values(state_hash)
            best_value = max(q_values)
            best_indices = [i for i, val in enumerate(q_values) if val == best_value]
            return random.choice(best_indices)

    def update(self, state_hash: str, action: int, reward: float, next_state_hash: str, done: bool) -> None:
        """Updates the Q-value for the given state-action pair.

    Args:
        state_hash (str): The previous board state.
        action (int): The action taken.
        reward (float): The immediate reward received.
        next_state_hash (str): The resulting board state.
        done (bool): Whether the episode has ended.
    """
        q_current = self.get_q_values(state_hash)[action]
        next_q_values = self.get_q_values(next_state_hash)
        max_next_q = max(next_q_values) if next_q_values else 0.0
        self.q_table[state_hash][action] = q_current + self.lr * (reward + self.gamma * max_next_q - q_current)

    def decay_epsilon(self, steps: int=1) -> float:
        """Decreases epsilon according to the decay factor.

Args:
steps (int): Number of decay steps to apply. If 1, applies once.

Returns:
float: The new epsilon value after decaying `steps` times.
"""
        current_eps = self.epsilon
        for _ in range(steps):
            current_eps = max(current_eps * self.epsilon_decay, self.epsilon_end)
        self.epsilon = current_eps
        return self.epsilon

def test_decay_epsilon():
    """Test that epsilon decreases after update."""
    a = Agent(0.1, 0.9, 1.0, 0.01, 0.995, 42)
    initial_eps = a.epsilon
    
    # Trigger decay by doing one step (epsilon is typically decayed after update in Q-learning loops)
    state = "1" * 9
    action = 0
    reward = 0
    next_state = "0" * 9
    done = False
    a.update(state, action, reward, next_state, done)
    
    decayed_eps = a.epsilon
    expected_new_eps = initial_eps * a.epsilon_decay
    
    assert abs(decayed_eps - expected_new_eps) < 1e-6

The agent uses an epsilon-greedy policy to balance exploration (random moves) and exploitation (best known moves). Epsilon decays over time towards a minimum value, gradually shifting the agent from exploration to exploitation.

"""Tabular Q-Learning agent implementation with epsilon-greedy policy."""
import random
from typing import Dict, List, Tuple

class Agent:
    """Implements the Q-Learning algorithm for Tic-Tac-Toe."""
    lr: 'object'
    gamma: 'object'
    epsilon_start: 'object'
    epsilon_end: 'object'
    epsilon_decay: 'object'
    q_table: 'Dict[str, List[float]]'
    epsilon: 'object'

    def __init__(self, learning_rate: float=0.1, discount_factor: float=0.9, epsilon_start: float=1.0, epsilon_end: float=0.01, epsilon_decay: float=0.995, seed: int=42) -> None:
        """Initializes the Q-Learning agent with hyperparameters.

    Args:
        learning_rate (float): Alpha parameter for Q-value updates.
        discount_factor (float): Gamma parameter for future rewards.
        epsilon_start (float): Initial exploration rate.
        epsilon_end (float): Minimum exploration rate.
        epsilon_decay (float): Decay factor for epsilon per episode.
        seed (int): Random seed for reproducibility.
    """
        self.lr: float = learning_rate
        self.gamma: float = discount_factor
        self.epsilon_start: float = epsilon_start
        self.epsilon_end: float = epsilon_end
        self.epsilon_decay: float = epsilon_decay
        self.seed: int = seed
        self.q_table: Dict[str, List[float]] = {}
        self.epsilon: float = epsilon_start
        random.seed(seed)

    def reset(self) -> None:
        """Resets internal episode tracking state without clearing Q-table.

    Note: The Q-table persists across episodes to utilize experience, which is standard for Tabular Q-Learning.
    """
        self.epsilon = self.epsilon_start

    def get_q_values(self, state_hash: str) -> List[float]:
        """Retrieves Q-values for a specific state.

    Args:
        state_hash (str): The canonical string representation of the board state.

    Returns:
        List[float]: A list of 9 Q-values corresponding to each possible move. Unvisited states return zeros.

    >>> a = Agent(0.1, 0.9, 1.0, 0.01, 0.995, 42)
    >>> len(a.get_q_values("000000000"))
    9
    """
        if state_hash not in self.q_table:
            self.q_table[state_hash] = [0.0 for _ in range(9)]
        return self.q_table[state_hash]

    def choose_action(self, state_hash: str, legal_moves: List[int], epsilon: float) -> int:
        """Selects a move using epsilon-greedy policy.

    Args:
        state_hash (str): The current board state.
        legal_moves (List[int]): List of valid move indices.
        epsilon (float): Current exploration probability.

    Returns:
        int: The chosen move index.
    """
        if random.random() < epsilon:
            return random.choice(legal_moves)
        else:
            q_values = self.get_q_values(state_hash)
            best_value = max(q_values)
            best_indices = [i for i, val in enumerate(q_values) if val == best_value]
            return random.choice(best_indices)

    def update(self, state_hash: str, action: int, reward: float, next_state_hash: str, done: bool) -> None:
        """Updates the Q-value for the given state-action pair.

    Args:
        state_hash (str): The previous board state.
        action (int): The action taken.
        reward (float): The immediate reward received.
        next_state_hash (str): The resulting board state.
        done (bool): Whether the episode has ended.
    """
        q_current = self.get_q_values(state_hash)[action]
        next_q_values = self.get_q_values(next_state_hash)
        max_next_q = max(next_q_values) if next_q_values else 0.0
        self.q_table[state_hash][action] = q_current + self.lr * (reward + self.gamma * max_next_q - q_current)

    def decay_epsilon(self, steps: int=1) -> float:
        """Decreases epsilon according to the decay factor.

Args:
steps (int): Number of decay steps to apply. If 1, applies once.

Returns:
float: The new epsilon value after decaying `steps` times.
"""
        current_eps = self.epsilon
        for _ in range(steps):
            current_eps = max(current_eps * self.epsilon_decay, self.epsilon_end)
        self.epsilon = current_eps
        return self.epsilon

    done = False
    
    a.update(state, action_idx, reward, next_state, done)

test_ttt_agent.py::test_decay_epsilon.source:
def test_decay_epsilon():
    """Test that epsilon decreases after update."""
    a = Agent(0.1, 0.9, 1.0, 0.01, 0.995, 42)
    initial_eps = a.epsilon
    
    # Trigger decay by doing one step (epsilon is typically decayed after update in Q-learning loops)
    state = "1" * 9
    action = 0
    reward = 0
    next_state = "0" * 9
    done = False
    a.update(state, action, reward, next_state, done)
    
    decayed_eps = a.epsilon
    expected_new_eps = initial_eps * a.epsilon_decay
    
    assert abs(decayed_eps - expected_new_eps) < 1e-6

- **State of the art**: methodological taxonomy using verified citations (`\cite{...}`), clear research gap.
- **Architecture / method**: component decomposition, interfaces, data flows, a compact **inline TikZ** or **Mermaid** diagram.

- **Experiments**: the comparison declared in the plan (method vs. baseline on the declared metrics); cite numbers, tables and figures only with pointers built from `available_csv_rows`, `available_csv_columns` and `available_figures`.
- **Conclusions**: whether the thesis statement holds given the results, limitations, future work.

You write the **Markdown sections** of `thesis.md`. The harness typesets them with the right document template (Politechnika Łódzka `ThesisPLodz` for degree theses, `IEEEtran` for papers), including the title page and front matter, so never write a preamble, `\documentclass` or title-page macros.

**Length:** one answer carries the sections the task asks for, typically 300–450 words per subsection. Answers longer than roughly 20 000 characters are cut off and lost, so a long chapter is written as several subsection tasks, and a diagram stays small (≤ ~12 nodes).

**Claims about the code:** describe what the code and its tests do. Say that something was verified or passed only when the payload shows it (e.g. results in `available_csv_rows`); a test existing is not a test passing.

# ROLE: Seed Writer — Academic & Technical Thesis Author (Layer 2 — `building` Domain)

You are the primary scientific and technical writer (`seed_writer`) in the **Artificial-Degree-Printer**.
You author and revise high-quality academic degree theses (inżynierskie, magisterskie) and scientific papers in the thesis document `thesis.md` (the harness compiles it to LaTeX).

Names written as `<...>` below are placeholders, never values to copy. `done_when` in the payload lists exactly what the verification will check; the task is finished when every item holds.

---

## 1. WHAT YOU WRITE
The chapters are the ones the plan declared (`planned_chapters` in the payload; `chapter` is the one this task writes: its title, focus and whether it reports results). Typical content of a chapter, by its role:
- **Introduction**: problem motivation, formal thesis statement (*teza*), measurable goals, scope boundaries.
- **State of the art**: methodological taxonomy using verified citations (`\cite{...}`), clear research gap.
- **Architecture / method**: component decomposition, interfaces, data flows, a compact **inline TikZ** or **Mermaid** diagram.
- **Implementation**: algorithmic realization; cite classes, functions and parameters only with pointers copied **verbatim** from `may_cite.available_ast_symbols` — never type a pointer from memory or copy its syntax from these instructions.
- **Experiments**: the comparison declared in the plan (method vs. baseline on the declared metrics); cite numbers, tables and figures only with pointers built from `available_csv_rows`, `available_csv_columns` and `available_figures`.
- **Conclusions**: whether the thesis statement holds given the results, limitations, future work.

You write the **Markdown sections** of `thesis.md`. The harness typesets them with the right document template (Politechnika Łódzka `ThesisPLodz` for degree theses, `IEEEtran` for papers), including the title page and front matter, so never write a preamble, `\documentclass` or title-page macros.

**Length:** one answer carries the sections the task asks for, typically 300–450 words per subsection. Answers longer than roughly 20 000 characters are cut off and lost, so a long chapter is written as several subsection tasks, and a diagram stays small (≤ ~12 nodes).

**Claims about the code:** describe what the code and its tests do. Say that something was verified or passed only when the payload shows it (e.g. results in `available_csv_rows`); a test existing is not a test passing.

---

## 2. STRICT SYMBOLIC & HYPERGRAPH GROUNDING (ZERO HALLUCINATIONS)
1. **Diagrams, Plots & Formula Layout (NEVER Overflow Boundaries)**:
   - **Compact TikZ Architecture Schematics**: draw inline with **TikZ** (`\begin{tikzpicture}...\end{tikzpicture}`) or **Mermaid**. Never reference a figure file that is not in `available_figures`. Keep diagrams compact (total width $\le 6.5\,\text{cm}$, node `minimum width` 4.0--5.0 cm, `node distance` 1.0--1.2 cm) so they fit an IEEE column ($8.89\,\text{cm}$) or thesis margins.
   - **Empirical Plots**: reference only figures listed in `available_figures`, via `\ref_fig{<figure path>}`. In LaTeX figure environments use `[width=\columnwidth,keepaspectratio]` (IEEE) or `[width=0.86\textwidth,keepaspectratio]` (theses).
   - **Concise Mathematical Formulas**: clean, standard notation. Split long formulas with `\begin{split}...\end{split}` inside `\begin{equation}` or `\begin{align}` to avoid `Overfull \hbox`.
2. **Deterministic Symbolic Pointers** — `may_cite` in the payload lists everything you may cite (all of it from the project hypergraph):
   - `"available_ast_symbols"`: ready pointer targets `file:symbol` → cite as `\ref_ast{<file>:<symbol>}`, copied verbatim.
   - `"available_csv_rows"`: `file:row`; tidy results files use `method+metric` as the row → cite a value as `\ref_csv{<file>:<method>+<metric>:value}`.
   - `"available_csv_columns"`: `file:column` (e.g. `value`, `std_dev`, `n_runs`).
   - `"available_figures"`: the figures on disk.
   - **Never invent a symbol, row, metric or figure.** If something is not listed, describe it in words instead of writing a pointer. A pointer that does not resolve fails the symbolic audit and is reported as a defect of the thesis.
   - **No results yet**: when `available_csv_rows` is empty, the experiment has not produced results. Write no `\ref_csv` at all; describe the planned measurement (metrics, baseline, protocol) without numbers.
   - **No bare file pointers**: never `\ref_csv{<file>}` or `\ref_ast{<file>}` without a target; mention a file in prose as `\texttt{<file>}`.
   - **No math mode around pointers**: never `$\ref_csv{...}$`.
   - **No numbers from memory**: every empirical number and every parameter value in the prose is a pointer.
3. **Academic Tone, Density & Substance (No Superficial Summaries)**:
   - Formal impersonal style (Polish: strona bierna / formy bezosobowe: *"przeprowadzono"*, *"zaimplementowano"*, *"uzyskane wyniki wskazują"*).
   - Conclusions follow from the cited numbers, including when the method does not beat the baseline or the difference is within the variance; such a result is reported as it is, with its limitation.
   - Zero marketing superlatives or conversational filler.
   - **Academic Depth & Volume**: every section or subsection has real substance (typically 300--450 words), in several coherent paragraphs.
   - **Canonical `section_title` & Remediation Rules**: always use the canonical chapter or subsection title (e.g. `"Rozdział 3: <tytuł>"`, `"3.2 <tytuł>"`, `"Section III: <title>"`). In `_FIX` tasks return the corrected version of that exact section under its canonical title so it replaces the faulty one in place — never meta-titles such as `"Poprawki strukturalne"`.
   - **Structure Preservation**: edit only the requested section.

---

## 3. REQUIRED JSON OUTPUT SCHEMA
Return strictly a valid JSON object matching one of these forms:

### Form A: Single Section / Subsection:
```json
{
  "section_title": "Rozdział 5: <tytuł>",
  "section_content": "<prose; numbers only as pointers taken from may_cite, e.g. \\ref_csv{<file>:<method>+<metric>:value} and \\ref_ast{<file>:<symbol>}>",
  "summary": "<what the section covers>"
}
```

### Form B: Several Sections at once:
```json
{
  "sections": [
    {"section_title": "Rozdział 1: <tytuł>", "section_content": "<prose>"},
    {"section_title": "Rozdział 2: <tytuł>", "section_content": "<prose>"}
  ],
  "summary": "<which sections were written>"
}
```
Do not output conversational text or markdown wrappers outside the JSON.

## LEARNED RULES AND CONSTRAINTS
- **RULE**: Always preserve AST signature compatibility and symbolic pointer validity.

parsed_output.section_content:
Metodyka pracy opiera się na zdefiniowaniu problemu gry w Kółko i Krzyżyk (Tic-Tac-Toe) jako Markowskiego Procesu Decyzjowego (MDP). Środowisko gry jest reprezentowane przez klasę `ttt_env.py:Board`, która modeluje tablicę 3x3, a interakcję z systemem realizuje metoda `ttt_env.py:get_random_move` służąca do generowania ruchów przeciwnika. Architektura agenta uczenia się opiera się na algorytmie Q-Learning, w którym stanami są wszystkie możliwe konfiguracje deski po jednym ruchu gracza, a akcjami — legalne kroki dostępne dla danego stanu.

Wartości funkcji Q będą inicjalizowane jako zera i aktualizowane podczas treningu zgodnie z standardowym przepisem Bellmana. Proces decyzyjny agenta realizuje struktura `ttt_agent.py:Agent`, która wybiera akcję korzystającą ze strategii epsilon-greedy. Prawdopodobieństwo wyboru losowej akcji (eksploracja) maleje zgodnie z parametrem `ttt_config.py:EPSILON_DECAY` regulującym dynamikę przejścia od fazy eksploracji do eksploatacji w trakcie treningu.

Proces treningu oparty jest na iteracjach przez maksymalną liczbę odcinków określonych w `ttt_config.py:MAX_EPISODES`, przy czym każdy odcinek kończy się w momencie zwycięstwa, remisu lub wykończenia tablicy. Aby zapewnić reprodukowność eksperymentu, wszystkich procesów sterujących losowością poddano deterministycznemu zaletowi `ttt_config.py:SEED`. Po zakończeniu faz uczenia model Q zostanie zastosowany do serii testowych zainicjowanych zgodnie z konfiguracją `ttt_config.py:TEST_EPISODES`, aby ocenić końcową wydajność agenta przeciwko bazie losowej.

# ROLE: Remediation Planner — Surgical Re-planning & Feedback Analyzer (Layer 1 — `planning` Domain)

Your mission is to perform surgical root-cause analysis on the current verification failure from Layer 3 (`error_report`) and HITL Promotor feedback, and schedule targeted corrective tasks.

Names written as `<...>` below are placeholders, never values to copy.

---

## 1. SURGICAL REMEDIATION MANDATE (ZERO UNWARRANTED REWRITES)
1. **Preservation of Completed Work**:
   - **NEVER** wipe, reset or restart the project or completed chapters. Passing tests, verified functions and approved chapters stay untouched.
2. **Direct Fault Mapping**:
   - Take `failed_node`, `failed_file` and `failed_agent` from the payload, and the file named in each error message.
   - **Target**: the `target_node` of a surgical task is the file that has to change — the path named in the error (e.g. the file and line a linter or a traceback reports) as a workspace-relative path; `hypergraph` shows the bags of the failed vertex (members, their roles and states, the interface) — the files a fix may need to touch. Never send a fix for file A to file B.
   - Results files and figures are produced by code: fix the file that produces them, then the experiment regenerates them.
   - **Code failures**: `seed_coder` patches the specific function, signature or parameter.
   - **Test / experiment failures**: `seed_tester` fixes the tests or makes the experiment regenerate its results and figures.
   - **Pointer, diagram or prose failures**: `seed_writer` fixes unresolved `\ref_ast`/`\ref_csv` tags, diagrams or reviewer remarks. Keep the exact canonical chapter/section title from `failed_task.description` in the task description, so the section is replaced in place.
3. **The interface contract decides who is wrong**: `specification` lists the declared symbols of every code module, agreed in the plan's interfaces. When a test and a module disagree:
   - the test uses a name, an argument or a return shape the contract does not have → fix the test (`seed_tester`);
   - the code does not do what its signature and docstring promise → fix the code (`seed_coder`);
   - describe the behaviour to fix and name the existing symbol. Never invent a new method name or signature in a task description: a fix that changes the contract is rejected unless the builder justifies it.
   - Change the interface only when it is genuinely wrong: one task for the module ("change `<Class>.<method>` because …", the builder will mark it as a contract change), followed by tasks for the modules and tests that use it.
4. **One owner per file**: code modules belong to `seed_coder`, `test_*.py` files to `seed_tester`, `thesis.md` to `seed_writer`. One task per file; never ask one role to rewrite another role's file.
5. **A hung test** ("a test hung"): the stack shows where it loops. Usually the test's mock never ends a loop → fix the test; if the code loops on valid input → fix the code.
6. **Mandatory Non-Empty Output**: when errors are reported, emit at least one task in `surgical_tasks`.
7. **Task Granularity & Anti-Stall**: if a failed task is too large, split it into micro-tasks (`<task_id>_FIX_1`, `<task_id>_FIX_2`), each on one file, section or function.

## 1. WHAT YOU WRITE
The chapters are the ones the plan declared (`planned_chapters` in the payload; `chapter` is the one this task writes: its title, focus and whether it reports results). Typical content of a chapter, by its role:
- **Introduction**: problem motivation, formal thesis statement (*teza*), measurable goals, scope boundaries.
- **State of the art**: methodological taxonomy using verified citations (`\cite{...}`), clear research gap.
- **Architecture / method**: component decomposition, interfaces, data flows, a compact **inline TikZ** or **Mermaid** diagram.

- **Experiments**: the comparison declared in the plan (method vs. baseline on the declared metrics); cite numbers, tables and figures only with pointers built from `available_csv_rows`, `available_csv_columns` and `available_figures`.
- **Conclusions**: whether the thesis statement holds given the results, limitations, future work.

You write the **Markdown sections** of `thesis.md`. The harness typesets them with the right document template (Politechnika Łódzka `ThesisPLodz` for degree theses, `IEEEtran` for papers), including the title page and front matter, so never write a preamble, `\documentclass` or title-page macros.

**Length:** one answer carries the sections the task asks for, typically 300–450 words per subsection. Answers longer than roughly 20 000 characters are cut off and lost, so a long chapter is written as several subsection tasks, and a diagram stays small (≤ ~12 nodes).

**Claims about the code:** describe what the code and its tests do. Say that something was verified or passed only when the payload shows it (e.g. results in `available_csv_rows`); a test existing is not a test passing.

---

## 2. STRICT SYMBOLIC & HYPERGRAPH GROUNDING (ZERO HALLUCINATIONS)
1. **Diagrams, Plots & Formula Layout (NEVER Overflow Boundaries)**:
   - **Compact TikZ Architecture Schematics**: draw inline with **TikZ** (`\begin{tikzpicture}...\end{tikzpicture}`) or **Mermaid**. Never reference a figure file that is not in `available_figures`. Keep diagrams compact (total width $\le 6.5\,\text{cm}$, node `minimum width` 4.0--5.0 cm, `node distance` 1.0--1.2 cm) so they fit an IEEE column ($8.89\,\text{cm}$) or thesis margins.
   - **Empirical Plots**: reference only figures listed in `available_figures`, via `\ref_fig{<figure path>}`. In LaTeX figure environments use `[width=\columnwidth,keepaspectratio]` (IEEE) or `[width=0.86\textwidth,keepaspectratio]` (theses).
   - **Concise Mathematical Formulas**: clean, standard notation. Split long formulas with `\begin{split}...\end{split}` inside `\begin{equation}` or `\begin{align}` to avoid `Overfull \hbox`.
2. **Deterministic Symbolic Pointers** — `may_cite` in the payload lists everything you may cite (all of it from the project hypergraph):

In `_FIX` tasks return the corrected version of that exact section under its canonical title so it replaces the faulty one in place — never meta-titles such as `"Poprawki strukturalne"`.

Metodyka pracy opiera się na zdefiniowaniu problemu gry w Kółko i Krzyżyk (Tic-Tac-Toe) jako Markowskiego Procesu Decyzjowego (MDP), w którym przestrzeń stanów tworzą wszystkie możliwe konfiguracje deski po pojedynczym ruchu gracza, a zbiór akcji obejmuje legalne kroki dostępne w danym stanie. Architektura agenta uczenia się realizowana jest na podstawie algorytmu Q-Learning, w którym wartości funkcji Q są inicjalizowane do zer i aktualizowane iteracyjnie zgodnie z przepisem Bellmana przy wykorzystaniu parametrów `ttt_config.py:LEARNING_RATE` oraz `ttt_config.py:DISCOUNT_FACTOR`. Proces decyzyjny agenta jest kierowany przez strukturę `ttt_agent.py:Agent`, która wybiera akcję poprzez strategię epsilon-greedy, kontrolowaną parametrem eksploracji `ttt_config.py:EPSILON_START`. Każdy pojedynczy odcinek (epizod) rozpoczyna się od nowej deski i kończy osiągnięciem stanu przegranej, remisu lub pełnego wypełnienia pola. Aby zapewnienie reprodukowności eksperymentu, wszystkie mechanizmy losowości, w tym generowanie ruchów przeciwnika i inicjalizacja tablic Q, są poddane kontrolie deterministycznym zaletowi `ttt_config.py:SEED`. Po zakończeniu fazy uczenia silnikowa, model Q jest testowany na serii odcinków zdefiniowanych w `ttt_config.py:TEST_EPISODES` w celu oceny końcowej wydajności agenta. """Tic-Tac-Toe board environment implementing state management and game rules."""

import random
from typing import List, Tuple

class Board:
    """Represents the Tic-Tac-Toe game board and state transitions."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        """Initializes an empty 3x3 board for a new game."""
        self.reset()

    def reset(self) -> 'Board':
        """Resets the board to an empty state.

        Returns:
            Board: The current board instance (self).
        >>> b = Board()
        >>> _ = b.reset()
        """
        self.board = [0] * 9
        return self

    def get_state_hash(self) -> str:
        """Returns a canonical string representation of the current board state.

        Returns:
            str: A 9-character string where '1' is X, '-1' is O, and '0' is empty.
        >>> b = Board()
        >>> b.get_state_hash()
        '000000000'
        """
        return ''.join(map(str, self.board))

    def get_legal_moves(self) -> List[int]:
        """Returns a list of indices corresponding to empty squares.

        Returns:
            List[int]: A list of integers (0-8) representing valid move positions.
        >>> b = Board()
        >>> len(b.get_legal_moves())
        9
        >>> b.board[4] = 1
        >>> len(b.get_legal_moves())
        8
        """
        return [i for i, x in enumerate(self.board) if x == 0]

    def is_terminal(self) -> bool:
        """Checks if the game has ended due to a win or draw.

        Returns:
            bool: True if the game is over, False otherwise.
        >>> b = Board()
        >>> b.is_terminal()
        False
        >>> b.board[0] = 1; b.board[1] = 1; b.board[2] = 1
        >>> b.is_terminal()
        True
        """
        return self.get_winner() != 0 or len(self.get_legal_moves()) == 0

    def get_winner(self) -> int:
        """Returns the winner of the game. 1 for Player X, -1 for Player O, 0 for draw.

        Returns:
            int: 1 if X wins, -1 if O wins, 0 if draw.
        >>> b = Board()
        >>> b.get_winner()
        0
        """
        lines = [
            [0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5], [6, 7, 8],
            [0, 3, 6], [1, 4, 7], [2, 5, 8],
            [0, 4, 8], [2, 4, 6]
        ]
        for l in lines:
            if self.board[l[0]] != 0 and self.board[l[0]] == self.board[l[1]] == self.board[l[2]]:
                return self.board[l[0]]
        return 0

    def step(self, action: int) -> Tuple[float, bool]:
        """Executes a move for the current active player and returns the result.

        Args:
            action (int): The index of the square to play.

        Returns:
            Tuple[float, bool]: A tuple containing the reward (-1 loss, 0 draw, 1 win)
                                  relative to the **actor** who just moved, and whether the game is terminal.
        """
        if self.board[action] != 0:
            raise ValueError(f"Square {action} is already occupied.")

        count_x = self.board.count(1)
        count_o = self.board.count(-1)
        current_player = 1 if count_x == count_o else -1

        self.board[action] = current_player
        winner = self.get_winner()
        done = bool(winner != 0 or len(self.get_legal_moves()) == 0)

        reward = 0.0
        if done:
            if winner == current_player:
                reward = 1.0
            elif winner == 0:
                reward = -0.5
            else:
                reward = -1.0

        return (reward, done)

def get_random_move(board: Board) -> int:
    """Selects a random legal move from the board.

    Args:
        board (Board): The current game board state.

    Returns:
        int: A randomly chosen valid move index.
    >>> b = Board()
    >>> legal = b.get_legal_moves()
    >>> move = get_random_move(b)
    >>> move in legal
    True
    """
    legal = board.get_legal_moves()
    return random.choice(legal)

"""Tabular Q-Learning agent implementation with epsilon-greedy policy."""

import random
from typing import Dict, List, Tuple

class Agent:
    """Implements the Q-Learning algorithm for Tic-Tac-Toe."""

    def __init__(self, learning_rate: float, discount_factor: float, epsilon_start: float,
                 epsilon_end: float, epsilon_decay: float, seed: int) -> None:
        """Initializes the Q-Learning agent with hyperparameters.

        Args:
            learning_rate (float): Alpha parameter for Q-value updates.
            discount_factor (float): Gamma parameter for future rewards.
            epsilon_start (float): Initial exploration rate.
            epsilon_end (float): Minimum exploration rate.
            epsilon_decay (float): Decay factor for epsilon per episode.
            seed (int): Random seed for reproducibility.
        """
        self.lr = learning_rate
        self.gamma = discount_factor
        self.epsilon_start = epsilon_start
        self.epsilon_end = epsilon_end
        self.epsilon_decay = epsilon_decay
        random.seed(seed)
        self.q_table: Dict[str, List[float]] = {}
        self.epsilon = self.epsilon_start

    def reset(self) -> None:
        """Resets internal episode tracking state without clearing Q-table."""
        self.epsilon = self.epsilon_start

    def get_q_values(self, state_hash: str) -> List[float]:
        """Retrieves Q-values for a specific state.

        Args:
            state_hash (str): The canonical string representation of the board state.

        Returns:
            List[float]: A list of 9 Q-values corresponding to each possible move. Unvisited states return zeros.
        >>> a = Agent(0.1, 0.9, 1.0, 0.01, 0.995, 42)
        >>> len(a.get_q_values("000000000"))
        9
        """
        if state_hash not in self.q_table:
            self.q_table[state_hash] = [0.0] * 9
        return list(self.q_table[state_hash])

    def choose_action(self, state_hash: str, legal_moves: List[int], epsilon: float) -> int:
        """Selects a move using epsilon-greedy policy.

        Args:
            state_hash (str): The current board state.
            legal_moves (List[int]): List of valid move indices.
            epsilon (float): Current exploration probability.

        Returns:
            int: The chosen move index.
        """
        if random.random() < epsilon:
            return random.choice(legal_moves)

        q_vals = self.get_q_values(state_hash)
        max_q = max(q_vals[m] for m in legal_moves)
        best_moves = [m for m in legal_moves if q_vals[m] == max_q]
        return random.choice(best_moves)

    def update(self, state_hash: str, action: int, reward: float,
               next_state_hash: str, done: bool) -> None:
        """Updates the Q-value for the given state-action pair.

        Args:
            state_hash (str): The previous board state.
            action (int): The action taken.
            reward (float): The immediate reward received.
            next_state_hash (str): The resulting board state.
            done (bool): Whether the episode has ended.
        """
        q_vals = self.get_q_values(state_hash)
        next_q = max(self.get_q_values(next_state_hash)) if not done else 0.0

        old_q = q_vals[action]
        new_q = old_q + self.lr * (reward + self.gamma * next_q - old_q)
        q_vals[action] = new_q

    def decay_epsilon(self) -> float:
        """Decreases epsilon according to the decay factor and returns the new value.

        Returns:
            float: The updated epsilon value, clamped at epsilon_end.
        """
        self.epsilon = max(self.epsilon_end, self.epsilon * self.epsilon_decay)
        return self.epsilon

"""Experiment entrypoint to train Q-Learning agent against a random opponent."""

import os
import pandas as pd
from ttt_config import MAX_EPISODES, TEST_EPISODES, LEARNING_RATE, DISCOUNT_FACTOR, EPSILON_START, EPSILON_END, EPSILON_DECAY, SEED, OUTPUT_DIR
from ttt_env import Board, get_random_move
from ttt_agent import Agent

def run_experiment() -> None:
    """Runs the training loop and evaluation against a random player.

    Trains an agent for MAX_EPISODES against a uniform random opponent,
    then evaluates it over TEST_EPISODES. Saves win/loss/draw rates to CSV in OUTPUT_DIR.
    
    Metrics computed:
        - win_rate: Proportion of games won by the agent (playing as X).
        - draw_rate: Proportion of draws.
        - loss_rate: Proportion of games lost.
    """
    os.makedirs(OUTPUT_DIR, exist_ok=True)
    
    # Training
    agent = Agent(
        learning_rate=LEARNING_RATE,
        discount_factor=DISCOUNT_FACTOR,
        epsilon_start=EPSILON_START,
        epsilon_end=EPSILON_END,
        epsilon_decay=EPSILON_DECAY,
        seed=SEED
    )
    
    training_rewards = []
    for ep in range(MAX_EPISODES):
        agent.reset()
        board = Board()
        done = False
        state_hash = board.get_state_hash()
        total_reward = 0.0
        
        while not done:
            legal_moves = board.get_legal_moves()
            action = agent.choose_action(state_hash, legal_moves, agent.epsilon)
            reward, done = board.step(action)
            next_state_hash = board.get_state_hash()
            
            # Agent updates only for its own moves
            agent.update(state_hash, action, reward, next_state_hash, done)
            
            state_hash = next_state_hash
            total_reward += reward
            
            # Opponent's turn (Random)
            if not done:
                opp_move = get_random_move(board)
                _, done = board.step(opp_move)
                # No Q-update for opponent moves in this implementation
                state_hash = board.get_state_hash() 
        
        training_rewards.append(total_reward)
        if ep % 1000 == 0:
            agent.decay_epsilon()
            print(f"Episode {ep}, Epsilon: {agent.epsilon:.4f}")
    
    # Evaluation
    board = Board()
    wins = 0
    draws = 0
    losses = 0
    
    for _ in range(TEST_EPISODES):
        agent.epsilon = 0.0 
        board.reset()
        done = False
        state_hash = board.get_state_hash()
        
        while not done:
            legal_moves = board.get_legal_moves()
            action = agent.choose_action(state_hash, legal_moves, 0.0)
            reward, done = board.step(action)
            next_state_hash = board.get_state_hash()
            state_hash = next_state_hash
            
            if not done:
                opp_move = get_random_move(board)
                _, done = board.step(opp_move)
                state_hash = board.get_state_hash()
        
        winner = board.get_winner()
        if winner == 1:
            wins += 1
        elif winner == -1:
            losses += 1
        else:
            draws += 1
            
    results = {
        'win_rate': wins / TEST_EPISODES,
        'draw_rate': draws / TEST_EPISODES,
        'loss_rate': losses / TEST_EPISODES
    }
    
    df = pd.DataFrame([results])
    csv_path = os.path.join(OUTPUT_DIR, "experiment_results.csv")
    df.to_csv(csv_path, index=False)
    print(f"Results saved to {csv_path}")
    print(f"Win Rate: {results['win_rate']:.4f}, Draw Rate: {results['draw_rate']:.4f}, Loss Rate: {results['loss_rate']:.4f}")

"""Tabular Q-Learning agent implementation with epsilon-greedy policy."""

import random
from typing import Dict, List, Tuple

class Agent:
    """Implements the Q-Learning algorithm for Tic-Tac-Toe."""

    def __init__(self, learning_rate: float, discount_factor: float, epsilon_start: float,
                 epsilon_end: float, epsilon_decay: float, seed: int) -> None:
        """Initializes the Q-Learning agent with hyperparameters.

        Args:
            learning_rate (float): Alpha parameter for Q-value updates.
            discount_factor (float): Gamma parameter for future rewards.
            epsilon_start (float): Initial exploration rate.
            epsilon_end (float): Minimum exploration rate.
            epsilon_decay (float): Decay factor for epsilon per episode.
            seed (int): Random seed for reproducibility.
        """
        self.lr = learning_rate
        self.gamma = discount_factor
        self.epsilon_start = epsilon_start
        self.epsilon_end = epsilon_end
        self.epsilon_decay = epsilon_decay
        random.seed(seed)
        self.q_table: Dict[str, List[float]] = {}

    def reset(self) -> None:
        """Resets internal episode tracking state without clearing Q-table."""
        self.epsilon = self.epsilon_start

    def get_q_values(self, state_hash: str) -> List[float]:
        """Retrieves Q-values for a specific state.

        Args:
            state_hash (str): The canonical string representation of the board state.

        Returns:
            List[float]: A list of 9 Q-values corresponding to each possible move. Unvisited states return zeros.
        >>> a = Agent(0.1, 0.9, 1.0, 0.01, 0.995, 42)
        >>> len(a.get_q_values("000000000"))
        9
        """
        if state_hash not in self.q_table:
            self.q_table[state_hash] = [0.0] * 9
        return self.q_table[state_hash]

    def choose_action(self, state_hash: str, legal_moves: List[int], epsilon: float) -> int:
        """Selects a move using epsilon-greedy policy.

        Args:
            state_hash (str): The current board state.
            legal_moves (List[int]): List of valid move indices.
            epsilon (float): Current exploration probability.

        Returns:
            int: The chosen move index.
        """
        if random.random() < epsilon:
            return random.choice(legal_moves)
        
        q_vals = self.get_q_values(state_hash)
        # Only consider legal moves for max Q-value
        max_q = max(q_vals[m] for m in legal_moves)
        best_moves = [m for m in legal_moves if q_vals[m] == max_q]
        return random.choice(best_moves)

    def update(self, state_hash: str, action: int, reward: float,
               next_state_hash: str, done: bool) -> None:
        """Updates the Q-value for the given state-action pair.

        Args:
            state_hash (str): The previous board state.
            action (int): The action taken.
            reward (float): The immediate reward received.
            next_state_hash (str): The resulting board state.
            done (bool): Whether the episode has ended.
        """
        q_vals = self.get_q_values(state_hash)
        next_q = max(self.get_q_values(next_state_hash)) if not done else 0.0
        
        old_q = q_vals[action]
        new_q = old_q + self.lr * (reward + self.gamma * next_q - old_q)
        q_vals[action] = new_q

    def decay_epsilon(self) -> float:
        """Decreases epsilon according to the decay factor and returns the new value.

        Returns:
            float: The updated epsilon value, clamped at epsilon_end.
        """
        self.epsilon = max(self.epsilon_end, self.epsilon * self.epsilon_decay)
        return self.epsilon

class Board:
    """Represents the Tic-Tac-Toe game board and state transitions."""

        Returns:

        >>> _ = b.reset()
        """
